# Pi-first integrated research-cycle contract

Sources: [PRD-010](../prd/PRD-010-pi-exa-integrated-research-cycle.md),
[feasibility and Jev evidence](../research/pi-exa-integrated-cycle-feasibility.md),
[issue #152](https://github.com/feniix/pi-extensions/issues/152).
Current source implements the merged v1.2 safety foundation, with an
[offline qualification/acceptance map](pi-exa-cycle-qualification.md).
Operator choices and delegated Jev selections are design evidence, not runtime
consent. PRD-010 v1.3 requires a guided background workflow before 6.1.0 is
published. The section below supersedes the foundation's manual normal-path
commands and submit-and-poll cycle execution. Later sections describe the
reusable foundation and historical slice decisions, not proof of new UX support.

## 6.1.0 target: separate proposal, submission, observation and delivery

### Boundaries

- **Planner/proposal:** assistant-operated non-spending start/update/preview.
  Guided intent routes explicitly to its cycle, with no standalone fallback.
  A human-readable proposal references the canonical request hash/revision
  internally; no second compiler or model-generated authorization object.
- **Approval adapter:** actual trusted host response creates durable scoped
  grants paired to that proposal. Reuse accounting/request/risk checks, without
  asking the user to copy hashes. Cancellation/unavailable UI/stale response
  fails closed. A conversational user request starts planning, not spending.
- **Submitter:** durable frozen intent and exclusive one-use create claim;
  one bounded create wait, remote-ID publication, monitor registration, then
  immediate acknowledgement. It does not wait for terminal completion.
- **Monitor:** host-owned lifecycle service with bounded same-ID GETs, no model
  polling loop, no create/continuation/replacement/cancel authority.
- **Reporter/delivery adapter:** terminal receipt and local processing precede
  durable notification scheduling. Wake the originating assistant at a safe
  turn boundary with an attempt reference, not raw vendor content as instructions.
  Reporting is read-only with respect to research spending.

Names above are architectural responsibilities, not settled public API names.
Do not implement by detaching an untracked promise from the existing blocking
tool or by telling the assistant to call that tool repeatedly.

### Reuse and changed behavior

Preserve the existing canonical project identity, private store, schema checks,
curated artifact/result policy, exact grants, monetary arithmetic, final dispatch
guards, late-observation accounting and immutable historical consent proofs.
Keep remote lifecycle, local processing, local monitoring and notice delivery as
separate state dimensions; a stopped monitor is not a failed Agent run.

Existing cycle submission currently inherits the shared wait/poll behavior.
The redesigned Pi path must not inherit cancellation-on-chat-interruption from
the blocking standalone path. Standalone/default-opt-out/MCP retain that
existing contract. Explicit recovery remains one bounded saved-run GET; it is
not the repeating monitor and must share safe observation coordination.

### Monitor ownership and persistence

Persist monitor intent bound to canonical project, cycle, attempt, saved remote
ID and originating session. Runtime ownership/generation fences permit at most
one authorized monitor per attempt across contenders. Use existing proven-dead
owner recovery principles, not age alone as takeover authority.

Keep network waits outside storage locks. Late genuine responses can settle only
their original attempt after detach/archive; stale callbacks cannot re-register
timers, notify a different session or submit work. Coalesce unchanged snapshots
without losing durability retries, changed costs, conflicts or late success.
Repeated explicit status/recovery must not spawn parallel polling loops.

Submission and monitor registration can fail independently. If create succeeded
but scheduling failed, retain and return the saved ID with “monitoring paused,”
not successful monitoring or submission failure. Bounded submission timeout
without an ID retains unknown intent. Late acknowledgement is persisted; attach
monitoring only if the originating ownership/context remains eligible.

Use bounded per-GET deadlines, non-overlapping checks and backoff; honor server
retry guidance when available. Numerical cadence/error limits are a design gate.
Auth/not-found/exhausted errors pause observation; remote outcome and financial
liability remain separate. No background action consumes replacement consent.

Shutdown stops local work; restart discovers resumable records without implicit
ownership or monitoring. Explicit user-requested assistant resume reacquires the
cycle and eligible monitor. Switch/fork/tree/archive fences local monitoring and
delivery; explain the pause. This is an in-process Pi feature, not an always-on
OS daemon or a promise of notifications after Pi exits.

### Durable completion delivery

Maintain a durable notice identity per attempt/terminal outcome, with originating
session, pending/delivered state and host acknowledgement when supported.
Persist the outcome first, then schedule delivery; record failure independently
from remote completion. Ordinary duplicate observations enqueue one notice.
Late additional financial facts update the record rather than erase the first
completion; separately material duplicate success remains reportable.

Do not hold the submission tool open or interrupt an active assistant response.
Deliver at a safe boundary or wake the idle origin session. For an unavailable/
detached origin, retain pending state for explicit resume; never redirect to the
currently active unrelated session. Check ownership again at actual delivery.

There is no assumed atomic transaction between filesystem publication and Pi
message delivery. Validate host acknowledgement semantics before choosing an
outbox protocol. Where acknowledgement is ambiguous across crash/restart,
surface pending/uncertain delivery and reconcile rather than claim exactly-once.
Completion of local processing/reporting is not evidence of criterion coverage.

### Implementation gates and verification

Before choosing tool schemas or scheduling APIs, inspect the pinned and supported
Pi extension APIs/examples for trusted confirmation, nonblocking host lifecycle,
safe-turn wakeup, session targeting and message acknowledgements. Verify Exa's
create/GET behavior without assuming SDK request abort or server idempotency.
Record capability evidence and limitations; reopen the design if a requirement
cannot be met. No new runtime dependency or model judgement service is implied.

Test first at real registered Pi tools/commands, host confirmation/lifecycle
boundaries, private filesystem controllers and mocked Exa endpoints. Use a
controllable pending job: submission must finish while the job is still pending,
a second user turn must remain possible, and terminal transition must cause
one safe completion delivery. Cover crash/fault injection, simultaneous runs,
ownership transfer, stale approval, unknown create and missed/ambiguous notices.
Finish with an interactive Pi smoke, not merely scripted callback invocation.
PRD scenarios 21–36 are the new release gates; old qualification does not satisfy
them. Live paid testing and publication require separate authority.

## Activation and host separation

Pi-only `--exa-enable-cycles` is initially disabled by default. When enabled,
an explicitly started/resumed cycle integrates automatically. Planning,
compilation, scoped accounting, one-use submission, explicit existing-run
recovery and funded retry/replacement are active under that opt-in. Unsupported
paths fail closed rather than silently falling back to standalone.
Completed-cycle views report recorded gaps/criteria and classified usage without
automatic satisfaction, verified billing or follow-up spending. Existing
standalone/MCP defaults and tool enablement remain unchanged.

Use a thin Pi registration/execution decorator to capture host context.
Inject optional host-neutral per-call raw-response/lifecycle observers into shared
helpers/factory, including late responses and cancel replies. MCP does not install
cycle behavior. Never use process-global mutable current-call context under concurrency.

## Identity, ownership, and durability

Project identity hashes canonical Git common directory, or canonical cwd outside
Git. Cycles have generated IDs, schema versions, monotonic plan revisions and
separate attempt IDs. Owner identity combines Pi session ID and runtime token.
Store curated JSON under the configured Pi agent directory's
`research-cycles/<project-id>/`, with restrictive directory/file permissions.

Start/switch/fork/clone/tree navigation/reload detaches the active pointer.
Explicit resume acquires exclusive ownership; a live owner blocks takeover.
Dead-owner recovery needs verified local liveness or explicit operator recovery,
not TTL alone. Unknown remote execution remains unknown after stale-owner recovery.
Old callbacks may reconcile their attempt under lock, but cannot submit more work
or overwrite another owner's plan. Compaction does not rewind durable state.

Short cross-process locks cover complete read/validate/reserve/durable-write
transactions, not network waits. Write/sync a same-directory temporary record,
atomically replace and sync its directory before submission. Outstanding durable
attempts and fenced ownership prevent duplicate automatic submissions.
Fail closed where filesystem durability/locking is unsupported.
Storage implementation chooses platform primitives and tests crash points;
it must not weaken the invariants.

Reset/archive detaches, retaining attempts, accounting, grants and liabilities.
It never cancels remote work or makes completed records executable.
Permanent deletion is outside this release.

## Commands and spending grants

- `/exa-research start <topic>` creates/activates without paid work.
- `/exa-research list` lists this project's saved cycles and liabilities.
- `/exa-research resume <cycle-id>` acquires ownership and displays existing scope,
  balance and completed/unknown/outstanding execution.
- `/exa-research approve <cycle-id> <amount>` issues an operator budget grant.
  Exception variants identify the exact operation/attempt and uncertainty/
  overspend/unknown-replacement scope.
- `/exa-research archive [cycle-id]` detaches/archives with outstanding-work warning.

Actual TUI/RPC confirmation responses can issue the same records. Cancellation,
decline or timeout does not grant permission. Headless calls pause without an
existing valid grant; no model-writable approval boolean is accepted.
Host command transport is the trusted operator boundary; arbitrary conversation
text or an assistant-supplied budget does not establish consent.

Grants record cycle/project, issuer session, command/dialog source, timestamp,
budget, tool/effort/provider/contact scope, and specifically named exceptions.
Resume preserves but never broadens grants. Scope changes require approval.
Exceptions cannot waive durable intent, ownership, conflicts or completion gates.

## Tools, attribution and conflicts

Keep the four planner names. In Pi cycle mode, step persists structured brief,
execution fields, input/exclusion rows, selected evidence and task schema, updating
revision; status exposes lifecycle/coverage/candidates/grants/ledger/next safe
action; summary previews the compiled artifact; reset archives/detaches.

Pi retrieval/research calls add `researchMode?: "active" | "standalone"`.
Omission uses the active cycle if present, otherwise retains standalone behavior.
Explicit active without a cycle is an error, not a standalone fallback.
Optional `cycleId` / `expectedRevision` assert the active target; they do not
implicitly resume or take over another cycle.
Standalone override denotes unrelated work, not permission to bypass recorded
cycle retries or outstanding restrictions. Code checks identifiable attempts;
semantic attribution remains assistant-owned.

In active Agent execution, query may be omitted because the plan is authoritative.
Explicit execution fields must match persisted values; otherwise update the plan
first. Scalars compare exactly; JSON object key order is canonicalized, array
order retained. No implicit additions, deep merges or execution-time plan mutation.
Exploratory retrieval queries remain search arguments, not final-brief overrides.

## Artifact and remote mapping

Artifact contains cycle/revision, brief, selected evidence, optional input/exclusion
records, task schema, execution controls and optional continuation. Hash canonical
JSON to identify the submitted artifact. Preview/execution share one compiler;
stale asserted revision/artifact fails before paid work.

Initial cycle efforts: minimal/low/medium/high/xhigh/auto; default medium.
Per-run `budget.maxCostDollars` is only for auto under documented server constraints,
not a hard cycle cap. Cycle max/ultra is deferred. Connect/contact work requires
explicit scope plus defensible add-on estimate or scoped uncertainty permission.

Require a persisted draft-07 root-object task schema. Missing/invalid schema blocks
readiness. Validate schema/results locally; do not impose Deep Search depth/property
limits on Agent. Task schema belongs to assistant/operator; package owns a stable
execution envelope. Validation failure after remote success is local processing
failure, not grounds to buy another synthesis.

Map brief and labeled selected URLs/provenance/notes to query text. Stable system
instructions treat notes as untrusted context, not instructions or verified facts.
Only explicit rows map to `input.data` / `input.exclusion`. No invented source-pack
API field. String metadata can identify cycle/revision/attempt, not ensure
idempotency or disclose private local paths/session identifiers.

Envelope retains attempt/artifact, remote ID/status/stop reason/error, task output,
raw field-level grounding, usage, classified costs, timestamps and local processing
outcome. Preserve failed/cancelled accounting and cancel's actual response.
Generated output alone never satisfies criteria.

## Budget, recovery and stopping

Keep published estimates, API retrieval estimates, Agent-reported cost/usage,
unknown liability and optional billing verification distinct. Reconcile reported
totals once; do not count components again or keep superseded reservations.
Unknown rates/extras/outstanding work require explicit assessment and scoped
approval where no defensible bound exists.

Freeze/write intent before create; capture IDs/raw results/late outcomes.
GET recovery never submits create. Unknown attempts block automatic replacement.
Confirmed failures can retry after budget reassessment; specifically approved
unknown replacements retain original liabilities and duplicate-outcome risks.
Remote success closes automatic submission eligibility even if local processing
fails. Recover/validate the existing result. Budget/time-limit completion reports
gaps and stops; another pass needs a newly authorized cycle.

## Slice ownership

| Slice | Contract delivered |
|---|---|
| #153 | JSON durability, lifecycle ownership, resume/archive |
| #154 | Schema validation, artifact compiler and conflict checks |
| #155 | Grants, budget assessments and raw/late retrieval usage |
| #156 | Candidates, curation and preserved provenance |
| #157 | Lifecycle observers, durable submission and result envelope |
| #158 | Remote inspection and interrupted/local-processing recovery |
| #159 | Confirmed-failure retry and scoped unknown replacement |
| #160 | Opt-in activation, guidance and whole-cycle verification |

No broad prefactor ticket is needed: add decorator/observer seams in first
consuming slices with standalone/MCP regression tests. Validator/lock utilities
and transport mechanics are implementation choices subject to these invariants
and repository dependency policy. Unavailable vendor guarantees use the defined
fail-closed/uncertainty paths, not invented support.

## #157 delegated execution decisions

The operator delegated design questions to Jev while authorizing continuation
through the backlog. Design-time `jev-1.13.0` selected these six decisions;
request/response evidence is retained outside git in
`/tmp/pi-exa-157-jev-{request,response}.json`. This is design evidence, not runtime
permission or proof of correctness.

- Extend the approved policy/compiler, real-filesystem controller and registered
  Pi testing seams with the public SDK lifecycle boundary. Mock only external
  create/get/cancel and filesystem crash points.
- Require explicit `web_research_exa` scope in a lifetime grant **and** one-use
  operator `approve-request` permission for the complete immutable compiled
  request. This binds effort, providers, continuation and contact-capable work
  without guessing intent from prose. The total assessment must cover any known
  fixed-effort base price; add-ons/auto remain scoped uncertainty, not vendor caps.
  Default exploratory grants still exclude Agent.
- Use call-local optional before-create/raw lifecycle observers, including late
  create/get/cancel replies. No global current-cycle state or inferred failure
  from formatted tool errors.
- Queued/running cost totals are provisional. Preserve the reservation until
  terminal receipts; interruption/missing terminal cost remains unknown.
- Remote completion irrevocably prevents another automatic run, even when local
  parsing/validation/persistence fails. Retain only validated structured task
  output, normalized credential-free citation metadata, numeric usage/cost and
  bounded processing diagnostics; never the full SDK response or invalid output.
  Exploration retains its separate metadata-only contract.
- Compile/assess/freeze/reserve durable intent in one owned transaction, then
  synchronize before create. Dispatch the exact preview request with a final
  synchronous ownership/generation/budget fence. Attempt identity is local, not
  an invented server idempotency key. #157 blocks replacement after any saved
  attempt; recovery/retry remain separate #158/#159 slices.

Agent price basis: [published pricing](https://exa.ai/docs/reference/pricing)
(last modified August 20, 2026): minimal $0.012, low $0.025, medium $0.10,
high $0.50, xhigh $1.00; contacts/providers are additional. SDK 2.23.0 and
the guide document beta `max`, while newer create docs list `ultra`; both remain
excluded from cycles. No live Agent call is authorized by these decisions.

A second design-time Jev round selected an explicit `failed` cycle lifecycle
for confirmed remote failed/cancelled outcomes, retaining the exact remote status
on its attempt. Local interruption remains `unknown`; cost liability is separate.
The #157 replacement block remains even after confirmed failure. Planning/grant
amendments for retries are a deliberate #159 change, not implicitly enabled here.
Evidence: `/tmp/pi-exa-157-jev-terminal-{request,response}.json`.

A third delegated Jev round reconciled the #157 explicit-call acceptance with
#160 complete-workflow rollout: expose only the safe single-attempt subset now
under the existing opt-in flag and exact operator permissions, with all
unavailable recovery/replacement paths failing closed. Do not invent a new flag
or test-only bypass. Evidence: `/tmp/pi-exa-157-jev-activation-{request,response}.json`.

## #159 delegated retry/replacement decisions

Jev selected a specific operator `approve-replacement` command binding project,
cycle, original unknown attempt/operation and the new immutable request hash.
It records literal duplicate-work/possible-additional-charge acknowledgment
and an original-liability assessment. Independent lifetime tool scope, a new
exact-request permission and fresh total-exposure assessment remain mandatory.
Assistant flags/amounts and Jev judgments never establish this consent.

Every unresolved unknown original needs a fresh unused exact-bound risk grant;
the exception cannot bypass unrelated live local execution, ownership,
receipt durability or submission guards. Consumed risk grants remain in
history and cannot authorize another replacement. Late successes remain
visible and stop further submissions, including duplicate outcomes following
a specifically approved exception.

Revised briefs remain drafts under failed/unknown lifecycle, with old frozen
artifacts/attempts/liabilities intact. Explicit retry/replacement preview and
execution use new revision/request identities; completion is never reopened
for further research. New cycles still require operator go-ahead.

Evidence: `/tmp/pi-exa-159-jev-{request,response}.json`.
The first pure history/risk policy slice is assessment-only; runtime retry,
operator commands and replacement execution remain gated pending controller
and registered Pi regressions.

The durable draft slice projects history from validated saved Agent attempts
and original ledger operations, not tool-supplied outcome flags. Editing and
preview preserve failed/unknown lifecycle and all prior contracts. Any success,
live intent/run, or unclassified history blocks a draft. Budget amendments and
new exact-request permissions may be recorded for an owned draft but do not
enable dispatch; the original single-attempt reservation guard remains.

Replacement records retain command/session provenance and a binding to the
simultaneously recorded original-operation liability permission, including its
assessment amount and issuance metadata. Publication/restore validate these
bindings. The controller rejects assessments below currently known costs,
including genuine provisional totals and the conservative published fixed-base
floor, and blocks conflicting receipts. These assessments are not vendor caps
or verified invoices. Late genuine completion still closes the entire cycle
without deleting its risk grants. Pi operator command registration, fresh
financial dispatch checks and risk consumption remain subsequent slices.

The intent slice adds explicit controller-only retry/replacement reservations.
Each gets a new operation and exact-request nonce after fresh total-exposure
assessment; specific risk IDs are consumed once in immutable intent metadata,
with source-attempt chronology and grant/request bindings checked on restore.
An intervening original-liability amendment invalidates an older paired risk
grant. Failed reservations do not consume grants. Aggregate lifecycle includes
all saved attempts: one local nondispatch cannot reopen unknown original work,
nor can an older failure hide a newer live intent. The intent-only milestone
kept transition SDK creates behind `RETRY_DISPATCH_GATED`; the subsequent
controller dispatch slice replaces that temporary gate with the fences below.
Registered Pi activation was implemented in the following explicit command/tool slice.

Jev selected frozen historical authorization proof rather than replaying today's
outcomes as though they existed at reservation. Each transition retains all
prior closed attempt facts/consumed risk IDs, known liability assessments, the
ordered recognized grant prefix and curated pre-intent monetary ledger.
Restore checks exhaustive immutable identities and compatible later outcomes,
replays then-current eligibility/funding/exposure and then-latest paired risk
liability, and requires the exact consumed source/risk arrays and a unique
request nonce covering the new hold. This is structural private-record proof,
not cryptographic authenticity or independent invoice verification.

Later genuine success, receipt growth/conflicts or appended operator liability
amendments must remain recordable/readable; they do not retroactively erase valid
historical consent. Future actual submission must separately recheck today's
success/concurrency/ownership/funding/liability state at its final guard.
Evidence: `/tmp/pi-exa-159-jev-restore-{request,response}.json`.

Grant issuance and intent/operation creation use a monotonic logical timestamp
computed from existing recognized events and wall time. It orders commands even
when the wall clock stalls or moves backward; it is not a lease timeout or a
vendor timestamp. The historical grant set must equal every recognized grant
issued strictly before the intent's cutoff, which must match its operation's
creation time. Truncation cannot hide an earlier amendment; extension cannot
turn a later nonce into historical funding. The restored liability minimum also
covers the immutable request's published fixed rate and frozen ledger receipts,
without treating later provisional growth as an invalid historical approval.

Controller dispatch rechecks original history, latest paired risk/liability,
held exact-request nonce, current total exposure, frozen artifact, owner and
generation both before the durable claim and in a synchronous no-await final
guard. The final guard opens a private owned regular record with no symlink
following, validates a fresh snapshot and never echoes malformed private JSON.
Known original success, another held local operation, grown liability or lost
scope/ownership blocks a new create without deleting its saved intent.

A same-process, operation-bound genuine completion latch also blocks creates
while the asynchronous receipt is publishing; successful durable publication
clears it, whereas unresolved local persistence failure remains conservative.
Across processes the fresh durable snapshot is the visibility/linearization
boundary; this is not a distributed transaction with vendor state. Local
nondispatch then releases only the new hold and preserves older unknown work.
Real-controller/mock-SDK regressions exercise funded failed retry and explicitly
approved unknown replacement with both late successes preserved and no third
create. No live paid SDK call or independently verified invoice is claimed.

The same-process completion latch uses the canonical real private-store
directory, not caller path spelling. A two-controller regression proves a
pending original completion blocks replacement through an equivalent relative
root after ownership handoff, before its asynchronous receipt publication.

Pi registration now exposes explicit `retry`/`replace` modes only on the opted-in
Agent tool and requires a resumed explicit cycle ID. The operator-only
`approve-replacement` command atomically issues the specific duplicate-work/
additional-charge acknowledgment and paired original liability assessment.
Each unknown original needs its own unused exact-new-request permission;
generic liability grants, assistant flags and ordinary active calls cannot
provide that consent. A preview displays the deterministic full SDK request
hash without creating a permission or reservation.

Registered-tool/mock-SDK regressions exercise failure plus freshly funded retry
and unknown work plus an amended draft/schema, explicit risk command and
replacement. The original late success validates against its original schema;
both results/charges survive, status and late progress surface duplicate
successes, and completion blocks a third call. Malformed/stale/underfunded risk
commands leave grants unchanged and never dispatch. Default-opt-out/standalone/
MCP behavior is unchanged. Full-feature review/publication remains pending.

## #158 delegated recovery decisions

Jev selected explicit Pi-only actions on existing tools: status `action=resume`
with a saved cycle ID, and Agent `researchMode=recover` for the existing
attempt. Default status remains inspection; neither startup nor saved-state
discovery implicitly resumes or grants spending consent. Standalone/MCP
contracts remain unchanged.

Recovery is one bounded SDK `agent.runs.get(id)` per explicit invocation, not
`create(previousRunId)`, an automatic polling loop or remote cancellation.
Local timeout/abort leaves the original attempt outcome uncertain; attached
call-local observers may still reconcile a late genuine reply. Missing IDs,
404/auth/network failures remain actionable unknown, not fabricated remote
failure. GET must bind the original saved attempt and validate/reprocess with
its frozen artifact/schema, without a new operation, grant or submission.
Source: Exa get-a-run primary documentation and pinned SDK 2.23.0.
Evidence: `/tmp/pi-exa-158-jev-{request,response}.json`.

The SDK inspection, original-attempt controller and registered Pi tool slices
are now implemented with offline regressions. Pi status discovers saved
summaries without activation; explicit resume acquires ownership, and explicit
Agent recovery performs one GET without a new attempt/reservation. Missing IDs
stay unknown, terminal completion cannot be undone, frozen assertions are
checked at preparation and actual GET preparation, and each GET observation
capability is one-use. Provider prose/raw responses remain outside durable
storage. The complete layer still requires fresh full-diff review; replacement
and whole-workflow rollout remain #159/#160.

## #157 review decisions

Fresh full-diff review identified two non-blocking display/diagnostic gaps.
Under the operator's delegated design authority, Jev selected a neutral
assessment-only `ledgerHealthy` status field (never a status `canDispatch`
claim) and a closed, package-owned remote-error summary instead of archiving
arbitrary vendor prose. Real per-request assessments retain `canDispatch`.
Evidence: `/tmp/pi-exa-157-jev-review-{request,response}.json`.

## #156 evidence implementation decisions

The operator approved metadata-first candidate retention and the public testing
seams: candidate normalization/curation policy, the real-filesystem cycle
controller, and registered Pi tools with mocked S

1	---
2	title: "Pi-first integrated Exa research-cycle contract"
3	prd: PRD-010
4	issue: 152
5	status: "6.1.0 guided background redesign; implementation design gates open"
6	---
7	
8	# Pi-first integrated research-cycle contract
9	
10	Sources: [PRD-010](../prd/PRD-010-pi-exa-integrated-research-cycle.md),
11	[feasibility and Jev evidence](../research/pi-exa-integrated-cycle-feasibility.md),
12	[issue #152](https://github.com/feniix/pi-extensions/issues/152).
13	Current source implements the merged v1.2 safety foundation, with an
14	[offline qualification/acceptance map](pi-exa-cycle-qualification.md).
15	Operator choices and delegated Jev selections are design evidence, not runtime
16	consent. PRD-010 v1.3 requires a guided background workflow before 6.1.0 is
17	published. The section below supersedes the foundation's manual normal-path
18	commands and submit-and-poll cycle execution. Later sections describe the
19	reusable foundation and historical slice decisions, not proof of new UX support.
20	
21	## 6.1.0 target: separate proposal, submission, observation and delivery
22	
23	### Boundaries
24	
25	- **Planner/proposal:** assistant-operated non-spending start/update/preview.
26	  Guided intent routes explicitly to its cycle, with no standalone fallback.
27	  A human-readable proposal references the canonical request hash/revision
28	  internally; no second compiler or model-generated authorization object.
29	- **Approval adapter:** actual trusted host response creates durable scoped
30	  grants paired to that proposal. Reuse accounting/request/risk checks, without
31	  asking the user to copy hashes. Cancellation/unavailable UI/stale response
32	  fails closed. A conversational user request starts planning, not spending.
33	- **Submitter:** durable frozen intent and exclusive one-use create claim;
34	  one bounded create wait, remote-ID publication, monitor registration, then
35	  immediate acknowledgement. It does not wait for terminal completion.
36	- **Monitor:** host-owned lifecycle service with bounded same-ID GETs, no model
37	  polling loop, no create/continuation/replacement/cancel authority.
38	- **Reporter/delivery adapter:** terminal receipt and local processing precede
39	  durable notification scheduling. Wake the originating assistant at a safe
40	  turn boundary with an attempt reference, not raw vendor content as instructions.
41	  Reporting is read-only with respect to research spending.
42	
43	Names above are architectural responsibilities, not settled public API names.
44	Do not implement by detaching an untracked promise from the existing blocking
45	tool or by telling the assistant to call that tool repeatedly.
46	
47	### Reuse and changed behavior
48	
49	Preserve the existing canonical project identity, private store, schema checks,
50	curated artifact/result policy, exact grants, monetary arithmetic, final dispatch
51	guards, late-observation accounting and immutable historical consent proofs.
52	Keep remote lifecycle, local processing, local monitoring and notice delivery as
53	separate state dimensions; a stopped monitor is not a failed Agent run.
54	
55	Existing cycle submission currently inherits the shared wait/poll behavior.
56	The redesigned Pi path must not inherit cancellation-on-chat-interruption from
57	the blocking standalone path. Standalone/default-opt-out/MCP retain that
58	existing contract. Explicit recovery remains one bounded saved-run GET; it is
59	not the repeating monitor and must share safe observation coordination.
60	
61	### Monitor ownership and persistence
62	
63	Persist monitor intent bound to canonical project, cycle, attempt, saved remote
64	ID and originating session. Runtime ownership/generation fences permit at most
65	one authorized monitor per attempt across contenders. Use existing proven-dead
66	owner recovery principles, not age alone as takeover authority.
67	
68	Keep network waits outside storage locks. Late genuine responses can settle only
69	their original attempt after detach/archive; stale callbacks cannot re-register
70	timers, notify a different session or submit work. Coalesce unchanged snapshots
71	without losing durability retries, changed costs, conflicts or late success.
72	Repeated explicit status/recovery must not spawn parallel polling loops.
73	
74	Submission and monitor registration can fail independently. If create succeeded
75	but scheduling failed, retain and return the saved ID with “monitoring paused,”
76	not successful monitoring or submission failure. Bounded submission timeout
77	without an ID retains unknown intent. Late acknowledgement is persisted; attach
78	monitoring only if the originating ownership/context remains eligible.
79	
80	Use bounded per-GET deadlines, non-overlapping checks and backoff; honor server
81	retry guidance when available. Numerical cadence/error limits are a design gate.
82	Auth/not-found/exhausted errors pause observation; remote outcome and financial
83	liability remain separate. No background action consumes replacement consent.
84	
85	Shutdown stops local work; restart discovers resumable records without implicit
86	ownership or monitoring. Explicit user-requested assistant resume reacquires the
87	cycle and eligible monitor. Switch/fork/tree/archive fences local monitoring and
88	delivery; explain the pause. This is an in-process Pi feature, not an always-on
89	OS daemon or a promise of notifications after Pi exits.
90	
91	### Durable completion delivery
92	
93	Maintain a durable notice identity per attempt/terminal outcome, with originating
94	session, pending/delivered state and host acknowledgement when supported.
95	Persist the outcome first, then schedule delivery; record failure independently
96	from remote completion. Ordinary duplicate observations enqueue one notice.
97	Late additional financial facts update the record rather than erase the first
98	completion; separately material duplicate success remains reportable.
99	
100	Do not hold the submission tool open or interrupt an active assistant response.
101	Deliver at a safe boundary or wake the idle origin session. For an unavailable/
102	detached origin, retain pending state for explicit resume; never redirect to the
103	currently active unrelated session. Check ownership again at actual delivery.
104	
105	There is no assumed atomic transaction between filesystem publication and Pi
106	message delivery. Validate host acknowledgement semantics before choosing an
107	outbox protocol. Where acknowledgement is ambiguous across crash/restart,
108	surface pending/uncertain delivery and reconcile rather than claim exactly-once.
109	Completion of local processing/reporting is not evidence of criterion coverage.
110	
111	### Implementation gates and verification
112	
113	Before choosing tool schemas or scheduling APIs, inspect the pinned and supported
114	Pi extension APIs/examples for trusted confirmation, nonblocking host lifecycle,
115	safe-turn wakeup, session targeting and message acknowledgements. Verify Exa's
116	create/GET behavior without assuming SDK request abort or server idempotency.
117	Record capability evidence and limitations; reopen the design if a requirement
118	cannot be met. No new runtime dependency or model judgement service is implied.
119	
120	Test first at real registered Pi tools/commands, host confirmation/lifecycle
121	boundaries, private filesystem controllers and mocked Exa endpoints. Use a
122	controllable pending job: submission must finish while the job is still pending,
123	a second user turn must remain possible, and terminal transition must cause
124	one safe completion delivery. Cover crash/fault injection, simultaneous runs,
125	ownership transfer, stale approval, unknown create and missed/ambiguous notices.
126	Finish with an interactive Pi smoke, not merely scripted callback invocation.
127	PRD scenarios 21–36 are the new release gates; old qualification does not satisfy
128	them. Live paid testing and publication require separate authority.
129	
130	## Activation and host separation
131	
132	Pi-only `--exa-enable-cycles` is initially disabled by default. When enabled,
133	an explicitly started/resumed cycle integrates automatically. Planning,
134	compilation, scoped accounting, one-use submission, explicit existing-run
135	recovery and funded retry/replacement are active under that opt-in. Unsupported
136	paths fail closed rather than silently falling back to standalone.
137	Completed-cycle views report recorded gaps/criteria and classified usage without
138	automatic satisfaction, verified billing or follow-up spending. Existing
139	standalone/MCP defaults and tool enablement remain unchanged.
140	
141	Use a thin Pi registration/execution decorator to capture host context.
142	Inject optional host-neutral per-call raw-response/lifecycle observers into shared
143	helpers/factory, including late responses and cancel replies. MCP does not install
144	cycle behavior. Never use process-global mutable current-call context under concurrency.
145	
146	## Identity, ownership, and durability
147	
148	Project identity hashes canonical Git common directory, or canonical cwd outside
149	Git. Cycles have generated IDs, schema versions, monotonic plan revisions and
150	separate attempt IDs. Owner identity combines Pi session ID and runtime token.
151	Store curated JSON under the configured Pi agent directory's
152	`research-cycles/<project-id>/`, with restrictive directory/file permissions.
153	
154	Start/switch/fork/clone/tree navigation/reload detaches the active pointer.
155	Explicit resume acquires exclusive ownership; a live owner blocks takeover.
156	Dead-owner recovery needs verified local liveness or explicit operator recovery,
157	not TTL alone. Unknown remote execution remains unknown after stale-owner recovery.
158	Old callbacks may reconcile their attempt under lock, but cannot submit more work
159	or overwrite another owner's plan. Compaction does not rewind durable state.
160	
161	Short cross-process locks cover complete read/validate/reserve/durable-write
162	transactions, not network waits. Write/sync a same-directory temporary record,
163	atomically replace and sync its directory before submission. Outstanding durable
164	attempts and fenced ownership prevent duplicate automatic submissions.
165	Fail closed where filesystem durability/locking is unsupported.
166	Storage implementation chooses platform primitives and tests crash points;
167	it must not weaken the invariants.
168	
169	Reset/archive detaches, retaining attempts, accounting, grants and liabilities.
170	It never cancels remote work or makes completed records executable.
171	Permanent deletion is outside this release.
172	
173	## Commands and spending grants
174	
175	- `/exa-research start <topic>` creates/activates without paid work.
176	- `/exa-research list` lists this project's saved cycles and liabilities.
177	- `/exa-research resume <cycle-id>` acquires ownership and displays existing scope,
178	  balance and completed/unknown/outstanding execution.
179	- `/exa-research approve <cycle-id> <amount>` issues an operator budget grant.
180	  Exception variants identify the exact operation/attempt and uncertainty/
181	  overspend/unknown-replacement scope.
182	- `/exa-research archive [cycle-id]` detaches/archives with outstanding-work warning.
183	
184	Actual TUI/RPC confirmation responses can issue the same records. Cancellation,
185	decline or timeout does not grant permission. Headless calls pause without an
186	existing valid grant; no model-writable approval boolean is accepted.
187	Host command transport is the trusted operator boundary; arbitrary conversation
188	text or an assistant-supplied budget does not establish consent.
189	
190	Grants record cycle/project, issuer session, command/dialog source, timestamp,
191	budget, tool/effort/provider/contact scope, and specifically named exceptions.
192	Resume preserves but never broadens grants. Scope changes require approval.
193	Exceptions cannot waive durable intent, ownership, conflicts or completion gates.
194	
195	## Tools, attribution and conflicts
196	
197	Keep the four planner names. In Pi cycle mode, step persists structured brief,
198	execution fields, input/exclusion rows, selected evidence and task schema, updating
199	revision; status exposes lifecycle/coverage/candidates/grants/ledger/next safe
200	action; summary previews the compiled artifact; reset archives/detaches.
201	
202	Pi retrieval/research calls add `researchMode?: "active" | "standalone"`.
203	Omission uses the active cycle if present, otherwise retains standalone behavior.
204	Explicit active without a cycle is an error, not a standalone fallback.
205	Optional `cycleId` / `expectedRevision` assert the active target; they do not
206	implicitly resume or take over another cycle.
207	Standalone override denotes unrelated work, not permission to bypass recorded
208	cycle retries or outstanding restrictions. Code checks identifiable attempts;
209	semantic attribution remains assistant-owned.
210	
211	In active Agent execution, query may be omitted because the plan is authoritative.
212	Explicit execution fields must match persisted values; otherwise update the plan
213	first. Scalars compare exactly; JSON object key order is canonicalized, array
214	order retained. No implicit additions, deep merges or execution-time plan mutation.
215	Exploratory retrieval queries remain search arguments, not final-brief overrides.
216	
217	## Artifact and remote mapping
218	
219	Artifact contains cycle/revision, brief, selected evidence, optional input/exclusion
220	records, task schema, execution controls and optional continuation. Hash canonical
221	JSON to identify the submitted artifact. Preview/execution share one compiler;
222	stale asserted revision/artifact fails before paid work.
223	
224	Initial cycle efforts: minimal/low/medium/high/xhigh/auto; default medium.
225	Per-run `budget.maxCostDollars` is only for auto under documented server constraints,
226	not a hard cycle cap. Cycle max/ultra is deferred. Connect/contact work requires
227	explicit scope plus defensible add-on estimate or scoped uncertainty permission.
228	
229	Require a persisted draft-07 root-object task schema. Missing/invalid schema blocks
230	readiness. Validate schema/results locally; do not impose Deep Search depth/property
231	limits on Agent. Task schema belongs to assistant/operator; package owns a stable
232	execution envelope. Validation failure after remote success is local processing
233	failure, not grounds to buy another synthesis.
234	
235	Map brief and labeled selected URLs/provenance/notes to query text. Stable system
236	instructions treat notes as untrusted context, not instructions or verified facts.
237	Only explicit rows map to `input.data` / `input.exclusion`. No invented source-pack
238	API field. String metadata can identify cycle/revision/attempt, not ensure
239	idempotency or disclose private local paths/session identifiers.
240	
241	Envelope retains attempt/artifact, remote ID/status/stop reason/error, task output,
242	raw field-level grounding, usage, classified costs, timestamps and local processing
243	outcome. Preserve failed/cancelled accounting and cancel's actual response.
244	Generated output alone never satisfies criteria.
245	
246	## Budget, recovery and stopping
247	
248	Keep published estimates, API retrieval estimates, Agent-reported cost/usage,
249	unknown liability and optional billing verification distinct. Reconcile reported
250	totals once; do not count components again or keep superseded reservations.
251	Unknown rates/extras/outstanding work require explicit assessment and scoped
252	approval where no defensible bound exists.
253	
254	Freeze/write intent before create; capture IDs/raw results/late outcomes.
255	GET recovery never submits create. Unknown attempts block automatic replacement.
256	Confirmed failures can retry after budget reassessment; specifically approved
257	unknown replacements retain original liabilities and duplicate-outcome risks.
258	Remote success closes automatic submission eligibility even if local processing
259	fails. Recover/validate the existing result. Budget/time-limit completion reports
260	gaps and stops; another pass needs a newly authorized cycle.
261	
262	## Slice ownership
263	
264	| Slice | Contract delivered |
265	|---|---|
266	| #153 | JSON durability, lifecycle ownership, resume/archive |
267	| #154 | Schema validation, artifact compiler and conflict checks |
268	| #155 | Grants, budget assessments and raw/late retrieval usage |
269	| #156 | Candidates, curation and preserved provenance |
270	| #157 | Lifecycle observers, durable submission and result envelope |
271	| #158 | Remote inspection and interrupted/local-processing recovery |
272	| #159 | Confirmed-failure retry and scoped unknown replacement |
273	| #160 | Opt-in activation, guidance and whole-cycle verification |
274	
275	No broad prefactor ticket is needed: add decorator/observer seams in first
276	consuming slices with standalone/MCP regression tests. Validator/lock utilities
277	and transport mechanics are implementation choices subject to these invariants
278	and repository dependency policy. Unavailable vendor guarantees use the defined
279	fail-closed/uncertainty paths, not invented support.
280	
281	## #157 delegated execution decisions
282	
283	The operator delegated design questions to Jev while authorizing continuation
284	through the backlog. Design-time `jev-1.13.0` selected these six decisions;
285	request/response evidence is retained outside git in
286	`/tmp/pi-exa-157-jev-{request,response}.json`. This is design evidence, not runtime
287	permission or proof of correctness.
288	
289	- Extend the approved policy/compiler, real-filesystem controller and registered
290	  Pi testing seams with the public SDK lifecycle boundary. Mock only external
291	  create/get/cancel and filesystem crash points.
292	- Require explicit `web_research_exa` scope in a lifetime grant **and** one-use
293	  operator `approve-request` permission for the complete immutable compiled
294	  request. This binds effort, providers, continuation and contact-capable work
295	  without guessing intent from prose. The total assessment must cover any known
296	  fixed-effort base price; add-ons/auto remain scoped uncertainty, not vendor caps.
297	  Default exploratory grants still exclude Agent.
298	- Use call-local optional before-create/raw lifecycle observers, including late
299	  create/get/cancel replies. No global current-cycle state or inferred failure
300	  from formatted tool errors.
301	- Queued/running cost totals are provisional. Preserve the reservation until
302	  terminal receipts; interruption/missing terminal cost remains unknown.
303	- Remote completion irrevocably prevents another automatic run, even when local
304	  parsing/validation/persistence fails. Retain only validated structured task
305	  output, normalized credential-free citation metadata, numeric usage/cost and
306	  bounded processing diagnostics; never the full SDK response or invalid output.
307	  Exploration retains its separate metadata-only contract.
308	- Compile/assess/freeze/reserve durable intent in one owned transaction, then
309	  synchronize before create. Dispatch the exact preview request with a final
310	  synchronous ownership/generation/budget fence. Attempt identity is local, not
311	  an invented server idempotency key. #157 blocks replacement after any saved
312	  attempt; recovery/retry remain separate #158/#159 slices.
313	
314	Agent price basis: [published pricing](https://exa.ai/docs/reference/pricing)
315	(last modified August 20, 2026): minimal $0.012, low $0.025, medium $0.10,
316	high $0.50, xhigh $1.00; contacts/providers are additional. SDK 2.23.0 and
317	the guide document beta `max`, while newer create docs list `ultra`; both remain
318	excluded from cycles. No live Agent call is authorized by these decisions.
319	
320	A second design-time Jev round selected an explicit `failed` cycle lifecycle
321	for confirmed remote failed/cancelled outcomes, retaining the exact remote status
322	on its attempt. Local interruption remains `unknown`; cost liability is separate.
323	The #157 replacement block remains even after confirmed failure. Planning/grant
324	amendments for retries are a deliberate #159 change, not implicitly enabled here.
325	Evidence: `/tmp/pi-exa-157-jev-terminal-{request,response}.json`.
326	
327	A third delegated Jev round reconciled the #157 explicit-call acceptance with
328	#160 complete-workflow rollout: expose only the safe single-attempt subset now
329	under the existing opt-in flag and exact operator permissions, with all
330	unavailable recovery/replacement paths failing closed. Do not invent a new flag
331	or test-only bypass. Evidence: `/tmp/pi-exa-157-jev-activation-{request,response}.json`.
332	
333	## #159 delegated retry/replacement decisions
334	
335	Jev selected a specific operator `approve-replacement` command binding project,
336	cycle, original unknown attempt/operation and the new immutable request hash.
337	It records literal duplicate-work/possible-additional-charge acknowledgment
338	and an original-liability assessment. Independent lifetime tool scope, a new
339	exact-request permission and fresh total-exposure assessment remain mandatory.
340	Assistant flags/amounts and Jev judgments never establish this consent.
341	
342	Every unresolved unknown original needs a fresh unused exact-bound risk grant;
343	the exception cannot bypass unrelated live local execution, ownership,
344	receipt durability or submission guards. Consumed risk grants remain in
345	history and cannot authorize another replacement. Late successes remain
346	visible and stop further submissions, including duplicate outcomes following
347	a specifically approved exception.
348	
349	Revised briefs remain drafts under failed/unknown lifecycle, with old frozen
350	artifacts/attempts/liabilities intact. Explicit retry/replacement preview and
351	execution use new revision/request identities; completion is never reopened
352	for further research. New cycles still require operator go-ahead.
353	
354	Evidence: `/tmp/pi-exa-159-jev-{request,response}.json`.
355	The first pure history/risk policy slice is assessment-only; runtime retry,
356	operator commands and replacement execution remain gated pending controller
357	and registered Pi regressions.
358	
359	The durable draft slice projects history from validated saved Agent attempts
360	and original ledger operations, not tool-supplied outcome flags. Editing and
361	preview preserve failed/unknown lifecycle and all prior contracts. Any success,
362	live intent/run, or unclassified history blocks a draft. Budget amendments and
363	new exact-request permissions may be recorded for an owned draft but do not
364	enable dispatch; the original single-attempt reservation guard remains.
365	
366	Replacement records retain command/session provenance and a binding to the
367	simultaneously recorded original-operation liability permission, including its
368	assessment amount and issuance metadata. Publication/restore validate these
369	bindings. The controller rejects assessments below currently known costs,
370	including genuine provisional totals and the conservative published fixed-base
371	floor, and blocks conflicting receipts. These assessments are not vendor caps
372	or verified invoices. Late genuine completion still closes the entire cycle
373	without deleting its risk grants. Pi operator command registration, fresh
374	financial dispatch checks and risk consumption remain subsequent slices.
375	
376	The intent slice adds explicit controller-only retry/replacement reservations.
377	Each gets a new operation and exact-request nonce after fresh total-exposure
378	assessment; specific risk IDs are consumed once in immutable intent metadata,
379	with source-attempt chronology and grant/request bindings checked on restore.
380	An intervening original-liability amendment invalidates an older paired risk
381	grant. Failed reservations do not consume grants. Aggregate lifecycle includes
382	all saved attempts: one local nondispatch cannot reopen unknown original work,
383	nor can an older failure hide a newer live intent. The intent-only milestone
384	kept transition SDK creates behind `RETRY_DISPATCH_GATED`; the subsequent
385	controller dispatch slice replaces that temporary gate with the fences below.
386	Registered Pi activation was implemented in the following explicit command/tool slice.
387	
388	Jev selected frozen historical authorization proof rather than replaying today's
389	outcomes as though they existed at reservation. Each transition retains all
390	prior closed attempt facts/consumed risk IDs, known liability assessments, the
391	ordered recognized grant prefix and curated pre-intent monetary ledger.
392	Restore checks exhaustive immutable identities and compatible later outcomes,
393	replays then-current eligibility/funding/exposure and then-latest paired risk
394	liability, and requires the exact consumed source/risk arrays and a unique
395	request nonce covering the new hold. This is structural private-record proof,
396	not cryptographic authenticity or independent invoice verification.
397	
398	Later genuine success, receipt growth/conflicts or appended operator liability
399	amendments must remain recordable/readable; they do not retroactively erase valid
400	historical consent. Future actual submission must separately recheck today's
401	success/concurrency/ownership/funding/liability state at its final guard.
402	Evidence: `/tmp/pi-exa-159-jev-restore-{request,response}.json`.
403	
404	Grant issuance and intent/operation creation use a monotonic logical timestamp
405	computed from existing recognized events and wall time. It orders commands even
406	when the wall clock stalls or moves backward; it is not a lease timeout or a
407	vendor timestamp. The historical grant set must equal every recognized grant
408	issued strictly before the intent's cutoff, which must match its operation's
409	creation time. Truncation cannot hide an earlier amendment; extension cannot
410	turn a later nonce into historical funding. The restored liability minimum also
411	covers the immutable request's published fixed rate and frozen ledger receipts,
412	without treating later provisional growth as an invalid historical approval.
413	
414	Controller dispatch rechecks original history, latest paired risk/liability,
415	held exact-request nonce, current total exposure, frozen artifact, owner and
416	generation both before the durable claim and in a synchronous no-await final
417	guard. The final guard opens a private owned regular record with no symlink
418	following, validates a fresh snapshot and never echoes malformed private JSON.
419	Known original success, another held local operation, grown liability or lost
420	scope/ownership blocks a new create without deleting its saved intent.
421	
422	A same-process, operation-bound genuine completion latch also blocks creates
423	while the asynchronous receipt is publishing; successful durable publication
424	clears it, whereas unresolved local persistence failure remains conservative.
425	Across processes the fresh durable snapshot is the visibility/linearization
426	boundary; this is not a distributed transaction with vendor state. Local
427	nondispatch then releases only the new hold and preserves older unknown work.
428	Real-controller/mock-SDK regressions exercise funded failed retry and explicitly
429	approved unknown replacement with both late successes preserved and no third
430	create. No live paid SDK call or independently verified invoice is claimed.
431	
432	The same-process completion latch uses the canonical real private-store
433	directory, not caller path spelling. A two-controller regression proves a
434	pending original completion blocks replacement through an equivalent relative
435	root after ownership handoff, before its asynchronous receipt publication.
436	
437	Pi registration now exposes explicit `retry`/`replace` modes only on the opted-in
438	Agent tool and requires a resumed explicit cycle ID. The operator-only
439	`approve-replacement` command atomically issues the specific duplicate-work/
440	additional-charge acknowledgment and paired original liability assessment.
441	Each unknown original needs its own unused exact-new-request permission;
442	generic liability grants, assistant flags and ordinary active calls cannot
443	provide that consent. A preview displays the deterministic full SDK request
444	hash without creating a permission or reservation.
445	
446	Registered-tool/mock-SDK regressions exercise failure plus freshly funded retry
447	and unknown work plus an amended draft/schema, explicit risk command and
448	replacement. The original late success validates against its original schema;
449	both results/charges survive, status and late progress surface duplicate
450	successes, and completion blocks a third call. Malformed/stale/underfunded risk
451	commands leave grants unchanged and never dispatch. Default-opt-out/standalone/
452	MCP behavior is unchanged. Full-feature review/publication remains pending.
453	
454	## #158 delegated recovery decisions
455	
456	Jev selected explicit Pi-only actions on existing tools: status `action=resume`
457	with a saved cycle ID, and Agent `researchMode=recover` for the existing
458	attempt. Default status remains inspection; neither startup nor saved-state
459	discovery implicitly resumes or grants spending consent. Standalone/MCP
460	contracts remain unchanged.
461	
462	Recovery is one bounded SDK `agent.runs.get(id)` per explicit invocation, not
463	`create(previousRunId)`, an automatic polling loop or remote cancellation.
464	Local timeout/abort leaves the original attempt outcome uncertain; attached
465	call-local observers may still reconcile a late genuine reply. Missing IDs,
466	404/auth/network failures remain actionable unknown, not fabricated remote
467	failure. GET must bind the original saved attempt and validate/reprocess with
468	its frozen artifact/schema, without a new operation, grant or submission.
469	Source: Exa get-a-run primary documentation and pinned SDK 2.23.0.
470	Evidence: `/tmp/pi-exa-158-jev-{request,response}.json`.
471	
472	The SDK inspection, original-attempt controller and registered Pi tool slices
473	are now implemented with offline regressions. Pi status discovers saved
474	summaries without activation; explicit resume acquires ownership, and explicit
475	Agent recovery performs one GET without a new attempt/reservation. Missing IDs
476	stay unknown, terminal completion cannot be undone, frozen assertions are
477	checked at preparation and actual GET preparation, and each GET observation
478	capability is one-use. Provider prose/raw responses remain outside durable
479	storage. The complete layer still requires fresh full-diff review; replacement
480	and whole-workflow rollout remain #159/#160.
481	
482	## #157 review decisions
483	
484	Fresh full-diff review identified two non-blocking display/diagnostic gaps.
485	Under the operator's delegated design authority, Jev selected a neutral
486	assessment-only `ledgerHealthy` status field (never a status `canDispatch`
487	claim) and a closed, package-owned remote-error summary instead of archiving
488	arbitrary vendor prose. Real per-request assessments retain `canDispatch`.
489	Evidence: `/tmp/pi-exa-157-jev-review-{request,response}.json`.
490	
491	## #156 evidence implementation decisions
492	
493	The operator approved metadata-first candidate retention and the public testing
494	seams: candidate normalization/curation policy, the real-filesystem cycle
495	controller, and registered Pi tools with mocked SDK responses/compiler previews.
496	
497	Cycle-attributed retrievals retain only stable candidate identities, bounded
498	titles/URLs, retrieval state and operation-bound provenance. Source bodies,
499	highlights, summaries, generated answers, processing rows and full SDK responses
500	are not automatically retained. Useful content notes are explicit curation.
501	Candidate capture does not select evidence or satisfy criteria.
502	
503	Candidate selection/rejection is an explicit planning update. Selection records
504	a planner source and a labeled execution-plan evidence reference; rejection
505	removes that candidate's selection without erasing its provenance. Existing
506	explicit source updates remain the external-evidence interface. Only selected
507	source facts and provenance enter previews; input rows remain explicit.
508	
509	Automatic capture requires the original active planning cycle and runtime
510	ownership. Detach/archive/ownership change prevents delayed callbacks from
511	changing evidence; late accounting remains a separate operation-bound capability.
512	The generation fence and final candidate namespace replacement are one synchronous
513	publication step under the filesystem lock. Revocation during asynchronous
514	preparation prevents publication; revocation after replacement does not undo
515	the already-published capture. File/directory synchronization remains required.
516	Candidate metadata is backward-compatible optional durable state, not a raw
517	response archive. Standalone, default opt-out and MCP calls do not capture it.
518	
519	## #155 accounting design grill
520	
521	The operator approved the accounting-policy, real-filesystem controller, and
522	registered Pi command/tool testing seams. Design-time Jev (`jev-1.13.0`) selected
523	the following choices in dependency-aware rounds; the operator confirmed the
524	resulting design before implementation. Jev is not a runtime dependency.
525	
526	- Approval amounts set a **total lifetime ceiling**, never additive credits.
527	- Call-local shared-tool factories carry operation-bound raw/late SDK observers.
528	- Default grants cover an explicit supported exploratory retrieval allowlist,
529	  not Agent, Connect/contact work or unknown extras.
530	- Package-owned published-price profiles record source, publication/review date,
531	  version and request-derived basis. They are estimates, not vendor billing caps
532	  or invoice verification. Unsupported pricing fails closed without a separately
533	  approved, immutable-request-bound uncertainty assessment.
534	- Checked integer micro-USD arithmetic rounds permission down and exposure up;
535	  invalid inputs and sum overflow fail closed.
536	- Owned, atomic assessments count reported usage, all pending estimates and
537	  explicitly assessed unknown liabilities. Durable operation identity/request
538	  hash and reservation precede SDK invocation; network waits never hold locks.
539	- Interrupted reservations remain possible liabilities. Unknown cost blocks
540	  autonomous spending until a valid receipt or operator permission naming that
541	  exact operation and assessed liability allowance. Permission does not change
542	  its classification to reported cost or cover future unknown operations.
543	- Genuine late callbacks reconcile only their saved operation, including after
544	  detach/archive/ownership changes. They cannot mutate plans, owners, lifecycle,
545	  grants or submission eligibility.
546	- Amendments preserve history and apply the latest ceiling/scope to new work;
547	  insufficient balance and overspend are surfaced before further dispatch.
548	- Only explicit valid API totals, including zero, resolve to API-reported usage.
549	  Reservations are replaced once; components are not counted again. Missing or
550	  malformed totals remain unknown. Conflicting receipts remain auditable and
551	  block new work rather than silently applying last-write-wins. Local formatting
552	  failures cannot discard genuine usage receipts.
553	- Versioned accounting records validate identities, money, scope and uniqueness.
554	  Opaque legacy data is preserved, never inferred as consent or zero liability.
555	- Release a reservation only when call-local facts prove SDK invocation never
556	  occurred. A local timeout, cancellation or error flag alone is insufficient.
557	
558	The 12 grill selections had selected-option probabilities 0.97–1.00; this is
559	design evidence, not proof of correctness. Offline regressions and independent
560	adversarial review remain required. Development approval grants no live spending.
561
