cat > /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-feniix-src-personal-pi-pi-extensions/90caff9b-07c1-45ca-be6f-308aff547939/scratchpad/pr-recovery.md <<'EOF'
## Summary

Fourth layer of the pi-exa 6.1.0 stack (#174, stacked on #179): background research survives local interruptions without duplicate remote work or lost outcomes. Restart discovers saved runs and pending notices; an explicit conversational resume picks them up.

**Package:** `@feniix/pi-exa` (opted-in Pi cycle path only; standalone, default-opt-out and MCP behavior unchanged).

## Changes

- `feat(pi-exa)`: recover monitoring and notifications across interruptions.
  - Explicit resume (`exa_research_status action=resume` or `/exa-research resume`) reacquires ownership, re-registers eligible paused monitors for the existing saved run (no create, no reservation), creates the notice missing for a terminal attempt whose scheduling crashed, and delivers pending or uncertain notices into the resuming session. Re-sent notices are labeled possible duplicates of the same single run; exactly-once is not claimed. Resume iterates saved attempts, so runs whose monitor registration failed after the create are recovered too.
  - Start discovery pauses only monitors whose cycle owner is absent or proven dead (`ESRCH`); a live owner elsewhere keeps observing and competing resumes are refused. Age alone never authorizes takeover.
  - A tick whose GET was in flight when the monitor was paused, archived or detached keeps the late original facts but schedules no notice for the detached context. Repeated resume never duplicates ticks; a detach latch lifts on a successful resume so delivery is reported honestly (`notice delivered` / `notice re-sent` / `notice pending`).
- `docs(pi-exa)`: README recovery section, planner skill guidance, changelog.

## Tests

`guided-recovery.test.ts` (registered extension, real private filesystem store, mocked Exa SDK; restart simulated by `session_shutdown` plus a fresh runtime over the same store): shutdown preservation and discovery without ownership or GETs; conversational resume with one delivery and one create; competing live runtime refused with no duplicate monitor; notice-scheduling crash recovered on resume; uncertain notice re-sent as a possible duplicate; late facts after archive without reactivation; duplicate-tick guard and tree navigation then resume; registration-failure run resumed; remote-ID publication crash kept unknown (`RECOVERY_UNAVAILABLE` names the missing ID, submission blocked); proven-dead owner paused on start and resumed by the next session; local-invalid result revalidated within the frozen contract with no consent inferred.

Run: `pnpm run check`, `pnpm run test`, `pnpm exec vitest run --coverage packages/pi-exa/__tests__`, `node scripts/check-release-changelog.mjs packages/pi-exa`.

## Honest limits

- Crash points are filesystem fault injection in one process, not separate-process or power-loss reproduction (as the qualification document already states).
- Live-owner refusal is proven in-process with a shared pid; dead-owner recovery via a written dead pid.
- Local interruption keeps an attempt `unknown` while its saved run ID, frozen artifact, grants and liability survive; the remote run is never declared failed locally.
- No interactive TUI run (#175).

## Decision requested

`researchMode=active` remains the foundation's blocking path for already opted-in callers; guided requests route to `submit`. Unchanged from #176–#179.

Closes #174.
EOF

Fourth layer of the pi-exa 6.1.0 stack (#174, stacked on #179): background research survives local interruptions without duplicate remote work or lost outcomes. Restart discovers saved runs and pending notices; an explicit conversational resume picks them up.

**Package:** `@feniix/pi-exa` (opted-in Pi cycle path only; standalone, default-opt-out and MCP behavior unchanged).

## Changes

- `feat(pi-exa)`: recover monitoring and notifications across interruptions.
  - Explicit resume (`exa_research_status action=resume` or `/exa-research resume`) reacquires ownership, re-registers eligible paused monitors for the existing saved run (no create, no reservation), creates the notice missing for a terminal attempt whose scheduling crashed, and delivers pending or uncertain notices into the resuming session. Re-sent notices are labeled possible duplicates of the same single run; exactly-once is not claimed. Resume iterates saved attempts, so runs whose monitor registration failed after the create are recovered too.
  - Start discovery pauses only monitors whose cycle owner is absent or proven dead (`ESRCH`); a live owner elsewhere keeps observing and competing resumes are refused. Age alone never authorizes takeover.
  - A tick whose GET was in flight when the monitor was paused, archived or detached keeps the late original facts but schedules no notice for the detached context. Repeated resume never duplicates ticks; a detach latch lifts on a successful resume so delivery is reported honestly (`notice delivered` / `notice re-sent` / `notice pending`).
- `docs(pi-exa)`: README recovery section, planner skill guidance, changelog.

## Tests

`guided-recovery.test.ts` (registered extension, real private filesystem store, mocked Exa SDK; restart simulated by `session_shutdown` plus a fresh runtime over the same store): shutdown preservation and discovery without ownership or GETs; conversational resume with one delivery and one create; competing live runtime refused with no duplicate monitor; notice-scheduling crash recovered on resume; uncertain notice re-sent as a possible duplicate; late facts after archive without reactivation; duplicate-tick guard and tree navigation then resume; registration-failure run resumed; remote-ID publication crash kept unknown (`RECOVERY_UNAVAILABLE` names the missing ID, submission blocked); proven-dead owner paused on start and resumed by the next session; local-invalid result revalidated within the frozen contract with no consent inferred.

Run: `pnpm run check`, `pnpm run test`, `pnpm exec vitest run --coverage packages/pi-exa/__tests__`, `node scripts/check-release-changelog.mjs packages/pi-exa`.

## Honest limits

- Crash points are filesystem fault injection in one process, not separate-process or power-loss reproduction (as the qualification document already states).
- Live-owner refusal is proven in-process with a shared pid; dead-owner recovery via a written dead pid.
- Local interruption keeps an attempt `unknown` while its saved run ID, frozen artifact, grants and liability survive; the remote run is never declared failed locally.
- No interactive TUI run (#175).

## Decision requested

`researchMode=active` remains the foundation's blocking path for already opted-in callers; guided requests route to `submit`. Unchanged from #176–#179.

Closes #174.
EOF

old_start=s.index('# Qualification boundary')
old_end=s.index('The opt-in Pi workflow is implemented behind')
new_head='''# Qualification boundary

**6.1.0 offline qualification.** PRD-010 v1.3 adds conversational setup/approval,
immediate submission acknowledgement, background monitoring, safe completion
delivery and recovery across interruptions (scenarios 21–36). This document maps
every scenario, 1–36, to regression evidence: the foundation suites below, the
guided suites added by #172–#174, and the #175 smoke that drives the production
extension in a real `pi --mode rpc` process against a controllable mock Exa HTTP
server. All evidence is mocked and offline; no paid Exa, Connect or model call was
made, and publication/release remain separate operator decisions.

**Evidence classes.** Keep these distinct when citing this document:

- *Mocked interactive smoke* (`guided-smoke.rpc.test.ts`): the real extension in a
  real Pi RPC process with the real `exa-js` SDK pointed at a mock HTTP server
  through `EXA_BASE_URL`; the RPC client is the trusted confirmation surface. It
  exercises the host protocol, not terminal rendering.
- *Registered-host regressions* (`guided-submission`, `guided-monitoring`,
  `guided-recovery`, `cycle-extension`): the real extension loaded through its
  entry point with a fake `ExtensionAPI`, the real private filesystem controller
  and a mocked `exa-js` module; restarts are simulated by `session_shutdown` plus a
  fresh runtime over the same store.
- *Host capability experiments* (`guided-prototype.test.ts`,
  `guided-prototype.rpc.test.ts`): the #171 prototype against Pi 1.1.0 SDK sessions
  and a real RPC process; design evidence, not production code.
- *Controller/policy units* (`research-cycles`, `research-artifacts`,
  `research-accounting`, `research-retry`, `agent-lifecycle`, `portable-tools`).

'''
s=s[:old_start]+new_head+s[old_end:]
# remove the earlier #171-only paragraph if still present
import re
s=re.sub(r"\*\*#171 prototype evidence \(design gates, not release qualification\)\.\*\*.*?until #172–#175\.\n\n", "", s, flags=re.S)
anchor='## Safety and verification limits'
table='''## Guided/background acceptance map (6.1.0)

Numbers match PRD-010 scenarios 21–36. Test names are searchable substrings.

| # | Regression evidence |
|---|---|
| 21 | Smoke “runs the whole journey without slash commands, schemas or hashes typed by the user”: the assistant drives `exa_research_status action=start`, `exa_research_step`, `mode=proposal` and `researchMode=submit` from a plain request; user prompts contain no slash command, schema or hash. Submission “creates a non-spending draft, renders a readable proposal”. |
| 22 | Submission “approves through the host dialog and returns the pending run ID” (dialog body carries topic, estimate, 10-minute timeout; dialog-sourced grants persisted) and “grants nothing when the dialog is declined or no trusted surface exists, and rejects forged approval inputs” (`APPROVAL_NOT_GRANTED`, `APPROVAL_UNAVAILABLE`, `EXECUTION_CONFLICT`, zero creates). Smoke “a cancelled dialog in the same journey submits nothing” over the real RPC protocol. Exploratory dialog: submission “discloses and approves optional exploratory retrieval through the dialog before dispatch”. |
| 23 | Submission “refuses a stale proposal after a plan edit before any dialog or create” (`PROPOSAL_STALE`, new proposalId after the edit). Controller `grantDialogApproval` asserts the artifact hash. |
| 24 | Submission normal path returns `runId` while the mocked run is `running` with zero GETs; smoke shows the second user prompt answered while HTTP GETs continue; monitoring “returns control with a registered monitor, observes with bounded GETs”. |
| 25 | Monitoring normal path: terminal GET → persisted outcome → one `exa-research-completion` notice sent with `triggerTurn` + `followUp` → `agent_settled` acknowledgement by the persisted entry → report; smoke shows the real wakeup turn calling `exa_research_status` and reporting after `server.complete`. No user prompt, one create, zero cancels. |
| 26 | Prototype SDK experiment “queues a completion that lands during an active response until the turn settles, and deduplicates repeated terminal observations” (host queue semantics, Pi 1.1.0). Monitoring normal path: explicit recover after completion creates no second notice. |
| 27 | Monitoring “pauses on local storage failure after a successful GET without an unhandled rejection”; recovery “recovers a terminal attempt whose notice scheduling crashed” and “keeps a remote-ID publication crash unknown”; recovery “re-sends an uncertain notice only on explicit resume, labeled as a possible duplicate, instead of claiming exactly-once”. Fault injection is in-process filesystem rename failure. |
| 28 | Submission “keeps an unacknowledged create unknown, saves a genuine late run ID on the original attempt and never resubmits” (`SUBMISSION_UNKNOWN`, `--exa-submit-timeout-ms`); recovery remote-ID crash (`RECOVERY_UNAVAILABLE` names the missing ID). |
| 29 | Monitoring “backs off transient GET errors, pauses when they are exhausted and pauses immediately on auth or not-found without fabricating remote failure” (`TRANSIENT_EXHAUSTED`, `AUTH`, `NOT_FOUND`; attempt stays `running`, no notice, no cancel). |
| 30 | Recovery “preserves state across shutdown, discovers without resuming, then an explicit conversational resume re-registers monitoring and delivers once” and “resumes monitoring for a saved run whose registration failed after the create”. |
| 31 | Recovery “refuses a competing live runtime and never duplicates an active monitor”, “pauses monitors of a proven-dead owner on start and lets the next session resume them”, “never duplicates ticks on repeated resume, and resume after tree navigation delivers a pending notice honestly”, “lets late original facts settle after archive without reactivating monitoring or delivering into the archived context”; monitoring “fences shutdown, restart and archive”. Prototype experiment “fences delivery after the runtime is invalidated and never redirects a pending notice to another session”. |
| 32 | Prototype SDK experiment “aborting the chat turn neither cancels the saved run nor lets the monitor create anything”; monitoring/recovery archive paths assert the outstanding-work warning and zero cancel calls; the mock HTTP server records no non-GET/create request in the smoke. |
| 33 | Monitoring “keeps two approved cycles in different sessions isolated: distinct runs, monitors, results and notices”. |

Approved submissions register a host-owned monitor that observes only the saved run with bounded, non-overlapping GETs (first after 5 s, ×1.5 backoff to 60 s with jitter; pauses after 8 transient failures or 10 min of silence, immediately on auth/not-found, and after 3 h). Monitoring has no create, retry, replace or cancel authority and runs only while Pi is open. Terminal facts, classified usage and the local validation outcome are persisted before one completion notice per attempt is recorded and delivered to the originating session through Pi's message queue (`exa-research-completion`), acknowledged by observing the persisted session entry. Shutdown, switch, fork, tree navigation and archive pause monitors; restart surfaces stale monitors and pending or uncertain notices without delivering them elsewhere. Registration failure after a create still returns the saved run ID with monitoring paused. New `--exa-monitor-interval-ms` flag (default 5000).

- **Monitoring and notification recovery across interruptions** (6.1.0, #174). Shutdown preserves run IDs, frozen contracts, grants, liabilities, monitor intent and notice state; restart discovers them without ownership, submission or monitoring, pausing only monitors whose owner is absent or proven dead. Explicit resume reacquires ownership, re-registers eligible paused monitors for the existing saved run, creates the notice missing after a scheduling crash and delivers pending or uncertain notices into the resuming session (re-sent notices are labeled possible duplicates; exactly-once is not claimed). Competing live runtimes are refused; late original facts settle after archive without reactivating monitoring or delivering into the archived context.

A production smoke drives the real extension in a real `pi --mode rpc` process with the real `exa-js` SDK pointed at a controllable mock Exa HTTP server through the new `EXA_BASE_URL` override: request → draft → readable proposal → trusted approval over the protocol → immediate saved run ID → continued conversation → background completion → report, plus a cancelled-dialog journey. Stale replacement consent is rejected before reservation without consuming permissions or changing saved history.

- **Exact conservative decimal micro-USD conversion** avoids binary floating-point boundary errors when flooring permission or ceiling exposure. Equivalent known terminal SDK receipts retain legitimate historical rounding without creating false conflicts; genuinely changed receipts remain auditable.

- **Storage and ownership availability:** atomically published PID/token transaction locks recover only proven-dead owners, use monotonic bounded contention waits and clean candidate links. Unverifiable/live locks are retained with actionable repair paths. Archiving unrelated history no longer revokes the active cycle, and readable discovery survives corrupt records while continuation attribution stays fail-closed.

}

lines: -- **Extension CLI flags are reachable by their documented names.** Pi registers flags by bare name and the CLI strips the leading dashes itself, so the `--exa-*` registrations were only reachable as `----exa-*`. `--exa-api-key`, `--exa-enable-advanced`, `--exa-enable-research`, `--exa-config-file`, `--exa-config`, `--exa-timeout-ms`, `--exa-research-timeout-ms`, `--exa-submit-timeout-ms` and `--exa-monitor-interval-ms` now parse as documented.

+- **Extension CLI flags are reachable by their documented names.** Pi registers flags by bare name and the CLI strips the leading dashes itself, so the `--exa-*` registrations were only reachable as `----exa-*`. `--exa-api-key`, `--exa-enable-advanced`, `--exa-enable-research`, `--exa-config-file`, `--exa-config`, `--exa-timeout-ms`, `--exa-research-timeout-ms`, `--exa-submit-timeout-ms` and `--exa-monitor-interval-ms` now parse as documented. Pi also applies flag values only after extension factories run, so tool enablement from `--exa-config-file`, `--exa-enable-advanced` and `--exa-enable-research` is now refreshed at `session_start`, registering newly enabled tools instead of silently ignoring the flags.

- **Replacement liability guards reuse the complete shared attempt floor**, including known receipt conflicts and the immutable fixed-effort base, instead of re-deriving a partial floor. Stale replacement consent is rejected before reservation without consuming permissions or changing saved history.

- **Exact conservative decimal micro-USD conversion** avoids binary floating-point boundary errors when flooring permission or ceiling exposure. Equivalent known terminal SDK receipts retain legitimate historical rounding without creating false conflicts; genuinely changed receipts remain auditable.

- **Storage and ownership availability:** atomically published PID/token transaction locks recover only proven-dead owners, use monotonic bounded contention waits and clean candidate links. Unverifiable/live locks are retained with actionable repair paths. Archiving unrelated history no longer revokes the active cycle, and readable discovery survives corrupt records while continuation attribution stays fail-closed.

## Summary

Top layer of the pi-exa 6.1.0 stack (#175, stacked on #180): qualify the complete guided background experience offline and reconcile the documentation. Release readiness only; no version bump, tag, release or publication is performed here.

**Package:** `@feniix/pi-exa`.

## Changes

- `fix(pi-exa)`: **CLI flags are reachable by their documented names.** Pi registers flags by bare name and strips the leading dashes itself, so the `--exa-*` registrations were only reachable as `----exa-*`. Pi also applies flag values only after extension factories run, so enablement from `--exa-config-file`, `--exa-enable-advanced` and `--exa-enable-research` is now refreshed at `session_start`. This is a user-visible CLI behavior change riding in a qualification PR: documented flags that did not parse on Pi 1.x now do.
- `feat(pi-exa)`: **`EXA_BASE_URL` override** (new environment input) pointing the Exa SDK at a self-hosted proxy or a controllable endpoint mock. Unset means the SDK default.
- `test(pi-exa)`: **production smoke** in a real `pi --mode rpc` process: the real extension and real `exa-js` against a mock Exa HTTP server, a scripted model reacting to actual tool results, and the RPC client as the trusted confirmation surface. Journeys: full request → draft → readable proposal → approval → immediate saved run ID → continued conversation while HTTP polling runs → background completion → wakeup → final report (no slash command, schema or hash typed by the user; one create; no cancel); completion during a streamed reply queued until the answer ends with exactly one notice; a cancelled dialog submitting nothing. The documented `--exa-config-file` flag is exercised in the real process.
- `docs(pi-exa)`: qualification map now covers PRD-010 scenarios 1–36 with evidence classes (mocked interactive smoke, registered-host regressions, host capability experiments, controller units) and an explicit list of unclaimed guarantees; PRD, architecture plan and qualification statuses updated; CONCEPTS gains "Background monitor" and "Completion notice"; changelog completed.

## Gates (current head, local)

`pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, `pnpm run check`, `pnpm run test` (1067 passed), `pnpm exec vitest run --coverage packages/pi-exa/__tests__` (lines 93%, branches 86%), `pnpm --filter @feniix/pi-exa run build:mcp`, `node scripts/check-release-changelog.mjs packages/pi-exa`, `pnpm run audit:workspaces` (no known vulnerabilities). The deferred version-bump stash is untouched.

## Honest limits

- The smoke exercises the RPC host protocol, not interactive TUI rendering.
- Crash points are in-process filesystem fault injection, not separate-process or power-loss reproduction.
- No exactly-once completion delivery is claimed; acknowledgement is by observing the persisted session entry. No cross-session delivery by design.
- Zero paid Exa, Connect or model calls; a live smoke needs separate operator authorization.

1. `researchMode=active` is retained as the foundation's blocking path while guided requests route to `submit`; hide it behind `submit` or keep it (unanswered since #176).
2. Merge bottom-up with `gh stack merge <pr> --yes`.
3. Version/date bump remains in the stash; release, tag and publish need separate authorization.

Closes #175.

-### Guided/background release acceptance (implemented; mapped in the qualification document)
21. “Research Laya versus Jev” starts a local guided draft, asks only material
clarification questions and requires no manual cycle command or schema.

- **Guided research from request through approved submission** (6.1.0, #172). `exa_research_status` `action: "start"` creates a non-spending cycle conversationally; `exa_research_summary` `mode: "proposal"` renders the readable scope/cost proposal and its `proposalId`; `web_research_exa` `researchMode: "submit"` asks the operator through Pi's confirmation dialog, records the lifetime scope/ceiling and one-use exact-request permission in one durable write, performs one bounded create and returns the saved Exa run ID while the job is still pending. Stale proposals, declined/dismissed/timed-out dialogs, headless modes and missing estimates fail closed and submit nothing; an unacknowledged create stays unknown and saves a genuine late run ID without resubmitting. Optional exploratory retrieval is disclosed and approved through the same dialog. New `--exa-submit-timeout-ms` flag (default 30000).

- **Background monitoring and completion delivery** (6.1.0, #173). Approved submissions register a host-owned monitor that observes only the saved run with bounded, non-overlapping GETs (first after 5 s, ×1.5 backoff to 60 s with jitter; pauses after 8 transient failures or 10 min of silence, immediately on auth/not-found, and after 3 h). Monitoring has no create, retry, replace or cancel authority and runs only while Pi is open. Terminal facts, classified usage and the local validation outcome are persisted before one completion notice per attempt is recorded and delivered to the originating session through Pi's message queue (`exa-research-completion`), acknowledged by observing the persisted session entry. Shutdown, switch, fork, tree navigation and archive pause monitors; restart surfaces stale monitors and pending or uncertain notices without delivering them elsewhere. Registration failure after a create still returns the saved run ID with monitoring paused. New `--exa-monitor-interval-ms` flag (default 5000).

- **Monitoring and notification recovery across interruptions** (6.1.0, #174). Shutdown preserves run IDs, frozen contracts, grants, liabilities, monitor intent and notice state; restart discovers them without ownership, submission or monitoring, pausing only monitors whose owner is absent or proven dead. Explicit resume reacquires ownership, re-registers eligible paused monitors for the existing saved run, creates the notice missing after a scheduling crash and delivers pending or uncertain notices into the resuming session (re-sent notices are labeled possible duplicates; exactly-once is not claimed). Competing live runtimes are refused; late original facts settle after archive without reactivating monitoring or delivering into the archived context.

-- **Offline qualification of the complete guided journey** (6.1.0, #175). A production smoke drives the real extension in a real `pi --mode rpc` process with the real `exa-js` SDK pointed at a controllable mock Exa HTTP server through the new `EXA_BASE_URL` override: request → draft → readable proposal → trusted approval over the protocol → immediate saved run ID → continued conversation → background completion → report, plus a cancelled-dialog journey. The qualification document maps PRD-010 scenarios 1–36 to executable evidence and states what remains unclaimed.

- **Read-only final cycle reports** with recorded criteria, evidence-reference diagnostics, gaps, assumptions, completion facts and classified usage. Integrated tool guidance and the planner skill describe the Pi workflow; the offline qualification document maps all 20 PRD-010 acceptance scenarios.

-- **Extension CLI flags are reachable by their documented names.** Pi registers flags by bare name and the CLI strips the leading dashes itself, so the `--exa-*` registrations were only reachable as `----exa-*`. `--exa-api-key`, `--exa-enable-advanced`, `--exa-enable-research`, `--exa-config-file`, `--exa-config`, `--exa-timeout-ms`, `--exa-research-timeout-ms`, `--exa-submit-timeout-ms` and `--exa-monitor-interval-ms` now parse as documented. Pi also applies flag values only after extension factories run, so tool enablement from `--exa-config-file`, `--exa-enable-advanced` and `--exa-enable-research` is now refreshed at `session_start`, registering newly enabled tools instead of silently ignoring the flags.

- **Replacement liability guards reuse the complete shared attempt floor**, including known receipt conflicts and the immutable fixed-effort base, instead of re-deriving a partial floor. Stale replacement consent is rejected before reservation without consuming permissions or changing saved history.

- **Exact conservative decimal micro-USD conversion** avoids binary floating-point boundary errors when flooring permission or ceiling exposure. Equivalent known terminal SDK receipts retain legitimate historical rounding without creating false conflicts; genuinely changed receipts remain auditable.

- **Storage and ownership availability:** atomically published PID/token transaction locks recover only proven-dead owners, use monotonic bounded contention waits and clean candidate links. Unverifiable/live locks are retained with actionable repair paths. Archiving unrelated history no longer revokes the active cycle, and readable discovery survives corrupt records while continuation attribution stays fail-closed.

+### Guided/background release acceptance (implemented; mapped in the qualification document)
21. “Research Laya versus Jev” starts a local guided draft, asks only material
clarification questions and requires no manual cycle command or schema.

- **Explicitly funded retry and replacement** through Agent `researchMode: "retry"` / `"replace"`. Each new attempt needs fresh exact-request funding; every unknown original additionally needs operator `approve-replacement` acknowledging duplicate work and possible additional charges. Historical contracts, consumed permissions and liabilities remain intact; genuine completion blocks further submissions and duplicate successes remain visible.

- **Guided research from request through approved submission** (6.1.0, #172). `exa_research_status` `action: "start"` creates a non-spending cycle conversationally; `exa_research_summary` `mode: "proposal"` renders the readable scope/cost proposal and its `proposalId`; `web_research_exa` `researchMode: "submit"` asks the operator through Pi's confirmation dialog, records the lifetime scope/ceiling and one-use exact-request permission in one durable write, performs one bounded create and returns the saved Exa run ID while the job is still pending. Stale proposals, declined/dismissed/timed-out dialogs, headless modes and missing estimates fail closed and submit nothing; an unacknowledged create stays unknown and saves a genuine late run ID without resubmitting. Optional exploratory retrieval is disclosed and approved through the same dialog. New `--exa-submit-timeout-ms` flag (default 30000).

- **Background monitoring and completion delivery** (6.1.0, #173). Approved submissions register a host-owned monitor that observes only the saved run with bounded, non-overlapping GETs (first after 5 s, ×1.5 backoff to 60 s with jitter; pauses after 8 transient failures or 10 min of silence, immediately on auth/not-found, and after 3 h). Monitoring has no create, retry, replace or cancel authority and runs only while Pi is open. Terminal facts, classified usage and the local validation outcome are persisted before one completion notice per attempt is recorded and delivered to the originating session through Pi's message queue (`exa-research-completion`), acknowledged by observing the persisted session entry. Shutdown, switch, fork, tree navigation and archive pause monitors; restart surfaces stale monitors and pending or uncertain notices without delivering them elsewhere. Registration failure after a create still returns the saved run ID with monitoring paused. New `--exa-monitor-interval-ms` flag (default 5000).

+- **Monitoring and notification recovery across interruptions** (6.1.0, #174). Shutdown preserves run IDs, frozen contracts, grants, liabilities, monitor intent and notice state; restart discovers them without ownership, submission or monitoring, pausing only monitors whose owner is absent or proven dead. Explicit resume reacquires ownership, re-registers eligible paused monitors for the existing saved run, creates the notice missing after a scheduling crash and delivers pending or uncertain notices into the resuming session (re-sent notices are labeled possible duplicates; exactly-once is not claimed). Competing live runtimes are refused; late original facts settle after archive without reactivating monitoring or delivering into the archived context.

+- **Offline qualification of the complete guided journey** (6.1.0, #175). A production smoke drives the real extension in a real `pi --mode rpc` process with the real `exa-js` SDK pointed at a controllable mock Exa HTTP server through the new `EXA_BASE_URL` override: request → draft → readable proposal → trusted approval over the protocol → immediate saved run ID → continued conversation → background completion → report, plus a cancelled-dialog journey. The qualification document maps PRD-010 scenarios 1–36 to executable evidence and states what remains unclaimed.

- **Read-only final cycle reports** with recorded criteria, evidence-reference diagnostics, gaps, assumptions, completion facts and classified usage. Integrated tool guidance and the planner skill describe the Pi workflow; the offline qualification document maps all 20 PRD-010 acceptance scenarios.

+- **Extension CLI flags are reachable by their documented names.** Pi registers flags by bare name and the CLI strips the leading dashes itself, so the `--exa-*` registrations were only reachable as `----exa-*`. `--exa-api-key`, `--exa-enable-advanced`, `--exa-enable-research`, `--exa-config-file`, `--exa-config`, `--exa-timeout-ms`, `--exa-research-timeout-ms`, `--exa-submit-timeout-ms` and `--exa-monitor-interval-ms` now parse as documented. Pi also applies flag values only after extension factories run, so tool enablement from `--exa-config-file`, `--exa-enable-advanced` and `--exa-enable-research` is now refreshed at `session_start`, registering newly enabled tools instead of silently ignoring the flags.

- **Replacement liability guards reuse the complete shared attempt floor**, including known receipt conflicts and the immutable fixed-effort base, instead of re-deriving a partial floor. Stale replacement consent is rejected before reservation without consuming permissions or changing saved history.

- **Exact conservative decimal micro-USD conversion** avoids binary floating-point boundary errors when flooring permission or ceiling exposure. Equivalent known terminal SDK receipts retain legitimate historical rounding without creating false conflicts; genuinely changed receipts remain auditable.

- **Storage and ownership availability:** atomically published PID/token transaction locks recover only proven-dead owners, use monotonic bounded contention waits and clean candidate links. Unverifiable/live locks are retained with actionable repair paths. Archiving unrelated history no longer revokes the active cycle, and readable discovery survives corrupt records while continuation attribution stays fail-closed.

Done. The whole #171 to #175 stack is implemented, pushed, and green in CI at every PR's current head.

**Pull requests, bottom to top, all ready for review and passing CI**
- #176 prototype and settled host contract: https://github.com/feniix/pi-extensions/pull/176
- #177 guided submission through approved dialog: https://github.com/feniix/pi-extensions/pull/177
- #179 background monitoring and completion delivery: https://github.com/feniix/pi-extensions/pull/179
- #180 recovery across interruptions: https://github.com/feniix/pi-extensions/pull/180
- #181 offline qualification of the complete journey: https://github.com/feniix/pi-extensions/pull/181

**What the stack delivers**
- A user says "research Laya versus Jev". The assistant starts a non-spending cycle, records the brief, renders a readable scope and cost proposal, and submits only after Pi's own confirmation dialog says yes. One create, run ID returned while the job is still pending.
- A host-owned monitor polls that saved run with bounded backoff while the user keeps chatting. Terminal facts persist first, then one completion notice wakes the originating session, acknowledged by observing the persisted session entry. Monitoring has no create, retry, replace or cancel authority.
- Shutdown, restart, archive, tree navigation and competing runtimes are fenced. Explicit resume reacquires ownership, re-registers paused monitors and reconciles pending or uncertain notices without claiming exactly-once.
- Two pre-existing bugs fixed along the way: Pi registers flags by bare name and applies values after factories run, so the documented `--exa-*` options did not parse on Pi 1.x before this stack. They do now, and tool enablement refreshes at `session_start`.

**Gates passed locally and in CI:** frozen install, lint, typecheck, 1067 tests, pi-exa coverage at 93% lines and 86% branches, MCP build, changelog check, dependency audit.

**Honest limits**
- The production smoke drives a real `pi --mode rpc` process with real `exa-js` against a mock HTTP server. It proves the host protocol, not terminal rendering.
- Crash points are in-process filesystem fault injection, not separate-process or power-loss reproduction.
- No cross-session delivery by design. Zero paid Exa or model calls were made.

**Decisions that are yours**
1. `researchMode=active` is kept as the foundation's blocking path while guided requests route to `submit`. You have not said whether to hide it behind `submit` instead; the plan flags this as pending.
2. Merge bottom-up with `gh stack merge <pr> --yes`, starting at #176.
3. The 6.1.0 version and date bump is still in your stash, untouched. Release, tag and publish need your separate go-ahead.

Base directory for this skill: /Users/feniix/.claude/skills/herdr

# Herdr

Herdr is a terminal multiplexer and runtime for coding agents. It organizes terminals into workspaces, tabs, and panes, detects agent identity and status, and exposes the running session through the `herdr` CLI.

Before issuing any control command, check that this agent is running inside a Herdr-managed pane:

```bash
test "${HERDR_ENV:-}" = 1
```

If the check fails, say that you are not running inside Herdr and stop. Do not inspect or control the focused Herdr session from outside Herdr.

When the check passes, the `herdr` binary in `PATH` talks to the running session. Use it to inspect neighboring work, create isolated terminal contexts, start agents and commands, read their output, and wait for state changes.

## Learn the current CLI

The installed binary is the authority for command syntax. Begin with:

```bash
herdr --help
```

Then print the relevant command group by running it without a subcommand:

```bash
herdr pane
herdr workspace
herdr worktree
herdr tab
herdr wait
herdr terminal
herdr notification
herdr integration
herdr session
```

Do not run bare `herdr` for discovery; it launches or attaches the TUI. Do not probe a mutating nested command by omitting arguments; some commands, including `herdr workspace create`, are valid with defaults and will execute. Use the command-group output above instead.

Most control commands print JSON. Read identifiers and state from those responses instead of predicting either one.

## IDs and current context

Public IDs are short stable handles:

- workspace: `w1`
- tab: `w1:t1`
- pane: `w1:p1`
- terminal: `term_...`

The encoded suffix can contain letters and can grow beyond one character. Treat every ID as an opaque string.

Closed tab and pane IDs are not reused and do not retarget later resources. A pane moved into another workspace receives a new public pane ID. Re-read create, split, move, list, or get responses after mutations; never construct an ID from a workspace or display number.

Herdr injects the caller's stable context into every managed pane:

```bash
printf '%s\n' "$HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID" "$HERDR_TAB_ID" "$HERDR_PANE_ID"
```

Prefer `--current` when a pane command should target the calling pane. Omitting a target can use the UI-focused pane, which may belong to the user or another client.

Discover live state with:

```bash
herdr workspace list
herdr tab list --workspace "$HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID"
herdr pane current --current
herdr pane list --workspace "$HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID"
```

## Control agents through panes

An agent runs inside a pane. Use the pane ID as the control target for agents, shells, servers, tests, and logs. This keeps spawning, input, reads, waits, and cleanup on one stable control surface.

Use workspace and tab commands for organization. Use worktree commands only when you intentionally want Herdr to create, open, or remove a Git checkout.

Pane records expose `agent`, `agent_status`, and native session metadata when available. Agent status is `idle`, `working`, `blocked`, `done`, or `unknown`.

`idle` and `done` are the same underlying semantic state with different attention state:

- `idle`: the agent is waiting and its result is considered seen.
- `done`: the agent finished and its result has not been seen.

An agent that first opens at its prompt reports `idle`, including in a background pane. After a working or blocked agent completes, it reports `done` when its tab or workspace is in the background. It reports `idle` when it completes in the active tab while the foreground client is focused. If the foreground client is explicitly unfocused, completion can become `done` even in the active tab.

Focusing a pane, switching to its tab, or regaining outer terminal focus marks the visible tab as seen, so `done` becomes `idle`. Switching away does not turn an existing `idle` status into `done`; `done` is created by a later completion while the pane is unseen. With no foreground client, a new completion in the globally active tab is treated as seen while completions in background tabs still become `done`.

## Start agents interactively

Default to a sibling pane in the current tab and current working directory. Do not create a workspace, tab, worktree, or different cwd unless the user explicitly requests that topology or location.

Honor a direction requested by the user. Otherwise inspect the caller pane's current rectangle:

```bash
herdr pane layout --pane "$HERDR_PANE_ID"
```

Split a wide pane to the right and a narrow or tall pane down. Avoid repeated same-direction splits that would create unusably narrow columns or short rows. Keep the user's focus in the calling pane:

```bash
herdr pane split --current --direction right --no-focus
```

Replace `right` with `down` when the layout calls for it.

Read `result.pane.pane_id` from the JSON response. Give the pane a useful label, then start the requested agent by running only its normal executable so its interactive TUI opens:

```bash
herdr pane rename <returned-pane-id> "reviewer"
herdr pane run <returned-pane-id> "codex"
```

Use the executable that belongs to the requested agent:

- Codex: `codex`
- Claude Code: `claude`
- pi: `pi`
- OpenCode: `opencode`
- OMP: `omp`

Do not pass the task as an argv prompt by default. Do not add non-interactive flags. Only change the normal interactive launch when the user explicitly asks for a different launch mode or command.

Inspect the pane after launch. If `agent_status` is not yet `idle`, wait for the idle transition. Once it is idle, submit the task with `pane run`:

```bash
herdr pane get <returned-pane-id>
herdr wait agent-status <returned-pane-id> --status idle --timeout 30000
herdr pane run <returned-pane-id> "Review the current diff and report only actionable findings."
```

Status waits match the current status immediately or wait for a future matching transition.

`pane run` sends the text and Enter together. Use it for initial prompts and follow-ups instead of coordinating `send-text` and `send-keys` separately.

For normal background work, wait for the agent to start working. If the pane remains in a background tab or workspace, wait for `done` before reading its transcript:

```bash
herdr wait agent-status <returned-pane-id> --status working --timeout 30000
herdr wait agent-status <returned-pane-id> --status done --timeout 120000
herdr pane read <returned-pane-id> --source recent-unwrapped --lines 120
```

If the user is watching that tab, completion reports `idle` instead, so wait for `idle`. Always treat either `idle` or `done` as completed when inspecting `pane get`; the difference is whether the result has been seen.

If a wait times out, inspect `herdr pane get <returned-pane-id>` and `pane read` before deciding what to do. A `blocked` agent needs input; an `unknown` pane may not yet contain a detected or integrated agent.

Submit follow-ups the same way:

```bash
herdr pane run <returned-pane-id> "Now check the failing test."
```

## Run an ordinary command in another pane

Split the calling pane using the same geometry rule without moving the user's focus:

```bash
herdr pane split --current --direction right --no-focus
```

Read the new `pane_id` from the JSON response, then run and inspect the command:

```bash
herdr pane run <returned-pane-id> "just test"
herdr wait output <returned-pane-id> --match "test result" --timeout 120000
herdr pane read <returned-pane-id> --source recent-unwrapped --lines 120
```

Inspect existing output before waiting for future output. A wait timeout exits with status `1`.

Use the read source that matches the task:

- `visible`: the current rendered viewport
- `recent`: recent scrollback as rendered, including soft wraps
- `recent-unwrapped`: recent scrollback with soft wraps joined; prefer it for logs and transcripts
- `detection`: the bottom-buffer snapshot used by agent detection

Use `--format ansi` when colors and terminal styling are evidence. Otherwise use text.

If the user explicitly asks for another tab, workspace, or worktree, discover that command group and use returned IDs. Do not infer a larger topology from a request to start an agent or command.

## Safety and coordination rules

- Use `--no-focus` for background work unless the user asked to switch context.
- Use `--current` or an explicit ID. Do not rely on another client's focused pane.
- Parse IDs from JSON responses. Do not derive them from sidebar order or examples.
- Inspect before waiting. Read current output first, then wait for the next state or output you expect.
- Do not close workspaces, tabs, panes, or sessions you did not create unless the user explicitly asked.
- Never run `herdr server stop` from an active session unless the user explicitly intends to stop the server and its pane processes.
- Never kill the main Herdr process. Use named test sessions for experiments that need an isolated server.

# i-have-adhd

The reader has ADHD. Output is not just brief. It is shaped so an ADHD brain can act on it.

## Persistence

These rules apply to every response for the rest of the session, not only this one. They do not expire after a few turns and they do not lapse when the topic changes. If you are unsure whether they still apply, they do.

Turn them off only when the reader says "stop adhd mode" or "normal mode". Confirm in one line, then return to your default style.

## What ADHD changes about reading

Five facts drive every rule below:

1. Working memory is small. Anything not on screen is forgotten. Do not ask the reader to "keep in mind X."
2. Knowing the answer is not doing the answer. The friction between "got it" and "done it" is where work dies.
3. Starting is the hardest step. The first action must be obvious, small, and doable now.
4. Time estimates feel uniform. "A bit of work" and "a few hours" register the same. Vague estimates fail.
5. Dopamine is scarce. Visible progress matters. Buried wins do not register.

## Rules

### 1. Lead with the next action

The first line is something the reader can do. Not context. Not a plan. The action.

Bad: "Let's think about this. Your auth flow has a few moving pieces..."
Good: "Run `npm install jsonwebtoken`, then edit `src/auth.ts:42`."

If the answer is a command, path, or snippet, it goes first. Prose comes after, if at all.

### 2. Number multi-step tasks

If the work takes more than one step, write a numbered list. Each step is one bounded action. No step contains "and then" twice.

Use the fewest steps that still work. Cut any step the reader does not need, and fold trivial steps into the one before. A short path finished beats a complete path abandoned.

Bad: "First open the file, find the function, swap it out, then run the tests."

Good:
```
1. Open `src/auth.ts`
2. Replace `verifyToken` (lines 42 to 58) with the snippet below
3. Run `npm test -- auth.spec.ts`
```

### 3. End with one concrete next action

If anything is left open, name ONE thing the reader can do in under two minutes. Even "open the file" counts.

Bad: "Hope that helps. Let me know if you want to dig deeper."
Good: "Next: run `npm test` and paste the first failing line."

### 4. Suppress tangents

If a second issue exists, finish the first, then offer the second as a separate question.

Bad: "Here's the fix. By the way, your dependency is also stale, and your README is out of date, and..."
Good: "Here's the fix. Separately: there is also a stale dependency. Want me to handle that next?"

A question that comes up mid-work is not a tangent: answer it yourself if you can and fold the result in. If it still needs the reader, surface it once, at the end.

### 5. Restate state every turn

The reader cannot hold "we are on step 3 of 5" between messages. Restate it.

Bad: "Done. Ready for the next part?"
Good: "Step 3 of 5 done: schema updated. Next: backfill the new column. Run the script?"

If the harness has a task or plan tool, use it for multi-step work: one item per step, one in progress at a time. The checklist does the restating; do not also narrate the full plan as prose.

### 6. Give specific time estimates

Vague estimates fail. Ballpark in concrete units.

Bad: "This will take some work."
Good: "About 15 minutes if tests already cover this. An afternoon if not."

### 7. Make completed work visible

Show what now works, in concrete terms. Do not bury wins in a recap.

Bad: "I've made some changes to the auth flow. Among other things..."
Good: "Login now works with magic links. Try: `npm run dev`, open `/login`."

### 8. Matter-of-fact tone for errors

Never use "Uh oh," "Oh no," or "There seems to be a problem." State cause and fix.

Bad: "Uh oh, the test is failing. There seems to be an issue..."
Good: "Test fails at `auth.spec.ts:42`: expected 200, got 401. Cause: missing auth header. Fix: add `Authorization: Bearer ${token}` to the request."

### 9. Cap lists to 5 items

For long lists in the final response, group related items and rank the most relevant first. Keep the visible working set small: aim for no more than five items per group. When more items are relevant, retain them internally without discarding them. Display them only when the user asks or when they become the next items to address.

Never omit relevant items when completeness matters. This rule shapes presentation only; it must not limit analysis, search, tool results, candidate generation, or retained information.

### 10. No preamble, no recap, no closing pleasantries

Forbidden openers: "Great question," "Let me...", "I'll...", "Sure!", "Looking at your...", "To answer your question..."

Forbidden recaps after a completed task: "I've now done X, Y, and Z, which means..."

Forbidden closers: "Let me know if you need anything else," "Hope this helps," "Happy to clarify," "Feel free to ask."

Start with the answer. End when the answer is done.

## When to break the rules

Override the defaults when:

1. User asks to "explain" or "walk me through." Explain fully. Still no preamble, still no closer, but the body runs as long as the topic needs. Add headers so the reader can skim back.
2. Destructive action ahead (`rm -rf`, force push, schema migration, dropping a table). Confirm before acting. Safety wins over brevity.
3. Debug spiral. If the last three turns have been "still broken," stop iterating on code. Name the assumption that might be wrong. Ask one diagnostic question.
4. Real ambiguity in the request. One short clarifying question beats guessing and rewriting.
5. A rule fights the task. When a rule would delete the answer itself, the task wins; the shape stays. Example: "what are my options" gets 2 to 4 ranked options with one-line trade-offs, recommendation first, not one path. The options are the answer.
6. A rule fights the harness. Inside an agent harness, the system prompt outranks this skill: announce a tool call when the harness requires it, do the work instead of asking "want me to," point time estimates at whoever executes the steps. Same principle as 5: the constraint wins, the shape stays.

## Pre-send check

Before sending, delete:

1. The first sentence if it announces what you are about to do.
2. The last sentence if it asks "anything else?" or recaps what just happened.
3. Any "by the way" sidebar.
4. Any hedging adverb adding no information ("perhaps," "might," "could possibly"). Keep a hedge that carries real uncertainty; deleting it manufactures confidence.
5. Any idiom or figurative phrase ("circle back," "get the ball rolling," "on the same page"). Replace with the literal action.

Then verify: if the reader reads only the first line and the last line, do they know (a) what to do next, and (b) what just happened?

If yes, send.

`active` is the old blocking way to run a cycle's Agent research. It submits the compiled request and then waits inside the tool call, polling until the run finishes, and cancels the remote run if you interrupt or the 180 s timeout hits.

How it differs from the new `submit`:

| | `active` (old) | `submit` (new, guided) |
|---|---|---|
| Approval | Operator types two slash commands first: `/exa-research approve` and `/exa-research approve-request <hash>` | Pi dialog, no commands or hashes |
| Behavior | Blocks the conversation until the run ends | Returns the run ID immediately, monitors in background |
| Interrupt | Cancels the remote run | Remote run keeps going |

Hiding it means: cycle research only through `submit`. Keeping it means: power users can still run the blocking, slash-command path.

Recommendation: hide. The PRD says 6.1.0 replaces blocking cycle execution, and nothing in the tests or docs depends on it. Standalone `web_research_exa` without a cycle is unaffected either way.

#### Compiled Agent attempts

With cycles enabled, the guided `researchMode: "submit"` path above obtains both
permissions through the confirmation dialog. The advanced `researchMode: "active"`
call keeps the foundation's blocking contract and executes the exact current
artifact after **both** operator permissions are recorded by command:

1. `/exa-research approve <cycle-id> <total-dollar-ceiling> web_research_exa`
   explicitly includes Agent in the lifetime tool scope (include other desired
   tools in the comma-separated scope; amendments replace the scope/ceiling).
2. `/exa-research approve-request <cycle-id> <request-hash> <assessed-dollars>`
   names the full immutable request displayed by the permission pause, including
   effort, providers, continuation and contact-capable query/output contract.

The request hash is distinct from the preview artifact hash. Request permission
is single-use; plan changes require a new exact-request assessment. An assessment
below the published fixed-effort base price fails closed. Contact/Connect extras
and metered work need the explicit full-request assessment; neither the estimate
nor the cycle ceiling is a vendor-enforced billing cap. Generic exploratory
grants still exclude Agent. No assistant-supplied flags or numbers grant consent.

'''## Known prototype simplifications

The prototype is design evidence for host capabilities, not a model of the production
store. A 2026-10-12 review recorded these deliberate gaps; the production implementation
(#172–#174) addresses each of them and the prototype is not maintained further:

- The prototype store is one JSON file rewritten whole without a lock or merge, and its
  attempt IDs are counter-based; an unreadable file is replaced by an empty store.
  Production uses the private, locked, validated per-cycle controller.
- Proposal consumption is checked before the dialog only, so parallel submits of one
  proposal could each create. Production rechecks inside the approval write and refuses
  a second attempt.
- A GET in flight across `session_shutdown` can finish its tick, and timer callbacks do
  not catch storage errors. Production fences ticks by monitor identity and pauses on
  storage failure.
- Every create rejection is classified unknown, and a late acknowledgement racing the
  deadline can be left unmonitored. Production keeps the conservative unknown rule but
  adopts genuine late acknowledgements into background monitoring.

  Production also acknowledges at session start and marks sent-but-unconfirmed notices
  uncertain.

'''### Lifecycle fences''',
'''### Review hardening (2026-10-12)

- Notices are claimed with a serialized `pending → sent` write before `sendMessage`, so a
  monitor tick and an explicit resume cannot both deliver one notice; a failed send
  releases the claim. A re-sent uncertain notice keeps a persisted `possibleDuplicate`
  label until it is delivered.
- A terminal outcome returned in a foreground tool result (explicit recover, or an
  acknowledgement that is already terminal) is never notified again: resume only reports
  terminal attempts that a background monitor owned, and recover acknowledges an existing
  monitor's notice with `channel: "tool-result"`.
- A genuine create acknowledgement that arrives after `SUBMISSION_UNKNOWN` (including an
  unknown original after a replacement) is adopted into background monitoring.
- Dialog approvals merge with the grant current at write time (never lowering a ceiling
  or scope), recheck for an existing attempt inside the write, and are not offered while
  overspend, conflicting receipts or unassessed unknown liabilities exist.
- Provider/contact requests have no package estimate: the operator assesses the exact
  request by command and the dialog confirms that existing funding.
- Monitors detach only on non-cancellable events (`session_shutdown`, `session_tree`); a
  vetoed switch or fork keeps observing. Ticks act only for the live entry of their key.

### Lifecycle fences''')])

## Summary

Seventh layer of the pi-exa 6.1.0 stack, stacked on #182. A fresh `/code-review` (high) of every PR in the stack (#176, #177, #179, #180, #181, #182) found 59 issues. All production findings are fixed here, at the top of the stack, against the final code; prototype (#176) findings are either fixed (overstated tests) or documented as known prototype limits.

**Package:** `@feniix/pi-exa`.

## Findings → fixes

**#177 / #182 guided consent**
- Submit without an active cycle fell through to a standalone paid Agent run → refused.
- Dialog shown and approval written before feasibility was known; approval could be recorded for a refused submission (also under concurrency) → attempt recheck inside the approval write, submitter preflight before the dialog, `DIALOG_APPROVAL_BLOCKED` for overspend / conflicting receipts / unassessed unknown liabilities (also for the exploration dialog, where a higher-priority scope reason hid them).
- Dialog grants could lower a wider ceiling or scope recorded meanwhile → merged with the grant current at write time.
- Provider/contact requests were funded at the base price → operator-assessed: no package estimate, operator records `approve` + `approve-request`, the dialog confirms.
- `SUBMISSION_NOT_DISPATCHED` told the assistant to submit again (impossible) → points at funded `retry`; a wait expiring before dispatch is now "not dispatched", not "unknown".
- Cycle mismatch reported as `AGENT_ATTEMPT_EXISTS` → mismatch reported first.
- Duplicated create building between lifecycles; dead `agentObserver`; per-call dispatch closure; redundant reads → shared builder, option removed, hoisted helper, terminal path reuses its snapshot.

**#179 / #180 / #182 background monitoring**
- Tick and resume could both deliver one notice → serialized claim (`pending → sent`) before sending; failed send releases it.
- Uncertain label lost after a failed re-send → persisted `possibleDuplicate`.
- Resume re-notified runs already reported in a tool result (terminal-on-ack, explicit recover) → resume only reports background-owned attempts; recover acknowledges an existing monitor's notice (`channel: "tool-result"`) and clears paused guidance.
- Late acknowledgement of an unknown original after replacement was never observed → genuine late create acknowledgements are adopted into monitoring.
- Storage failure in the transient branch killed the monitor silently → any storage failure in a tick pauses (`STORAGE`).
- Stale ticks could reschedule or pause a re-registered monitor → ticks act only for the live entry of their key.
- Resume of a dead owner's live monitor kept the old origin and lifetime → taken over by the resuming session.
- One failing attempt aborted the whole resume → per-attempt isolation.
- Vetoed switch/fork paused every monitor → detach only on `session_shutdown` / `session_tree`.
- Start paused other live runtimes' monitors and warned about foreign notices forever → live owners left alone; warnings only for this session's undelivered notices, after acknowledgement.
- First backoff step repeated the initial delay → 5 s, 7.5 s, 11.25 s …; cap never below the initial delay.
- Ack cache never populated; duplicated liveness probe and notice construction; dead code → fixed / shared helpers.

**#181 flags and fixtures**
- Late flags never reached factory-registered tools (timeouts), config-disabled tools stayed registered unwrapped, planner tools split across plans → call-time timeouts, hidden withdrawal, one shared planner.
- Deprecation warning on every call → once. `EXA_BASE_URL` unvalidated → absolute http(s) required.
- Smoke sync point matched old records; `RpcPi.stop` removed files while the child ran; mock counted unexpected GETs as monitoring → fixed.

**#176 prototype** — dedup/backoff tests asserted less than claimed → fixed or claim dropped; the remaining prototype simplifications are listed in the capability research doc.

**Restored coverage from #182**: interrupted-liability recovery regression; exact projection count.

## Accepted residuals (documented in the plan)

- Approval write and attempt reservation are two serialized transactions; a retry landing between them can still leave a recorded approval.
- A late terminal acknowledgement after its cycle detached cannot register a monitor record; the outcome is retained and shown by status, without a notice.
- Owner liveness is pid-based; pid reuse after a crash is the foundation's existing limit.

## Gates (local)

`pnpm run check`, `pnpm run test` (1087 passed), pi-exa coverage (lines 93.6%, branches 86.7%), MCP build, changelog check, audit. Stash untouched.

- `SUBMISSION_NOT_DISPATCHED` told the assistant to submit again (impossible) → points at funded `retry`; a wait expiring before dispatch is now "not dispatched", not "unknown".
- Cycle mismatch reported as `AGENT_ATTEMPT_EXISTS` → mismatch reported first.
- Duplicated create building between lifecycles; dead `agentObserver`; per-call dispatch closure; redundant reads → shared builder, option removed, hoisted helper, terminal path reuses its snapshot.

**#179 / #180 / #182 background monitoring**
- Tick and resume could both deliver one notice → serialized claim (`pending → sent`) before sending; failed send releases it.
- Uncertain label lost after a failed re-send → persisted `possibleDuplicate`.
- Resume re-notified runs already reported in a tool result (terminal-on-ack, explicit recover) → resume only reports background-owned attempts; recover acknowledges an existing monitor's notice (`channel: "tool-result"`) and clears paused guidance.
- Late acknowledgement of an unknown original after replacement was never observed → genuine late create acknowledgements are adopted into monitoring.
- Storage failure in the transient branch killed the monitor silently → any storage failure in a tick pauses (`STORAGE`).
- Stale ticks could reschedule or pause a re-registered monitor → ticks act only for the live entry of their key.
- Resume of a dead owner's live monitor kept the old origin and lifetime → taken over by the resuming session.
- One failing attempt aborted the whole resume → per-attempt isolation.
- Vetoed switch/fork paused every monitor → detach only on `session_shutdown` / `session_tree`.
- Start paused other live runtimes' monitors and warned about foreign notices forever → live owners left alone; warnings only for this session's undelivered notices, after acknowledgement.
- First backoff step repeated the initial delay → 5 s, 7.5 s, 11.25 s …; cap never below the initial delay.
- Ack cache never populated; duplicated liveness probe and notice construction; dead code → fixed / shared helpers.

**#181 flags and fixtures**
- Late flags never reached factory-registered tools (timeouts), config-disabled tools stayed registered unwrapped, planner tools split across plans → call-time timeouts, hidden withdrawal, one shared planner.
- Deprecation warning on every call → once. `EXA_BASE_URL` unvalidated → absolute http(s) required.
- Smoke sync point matched old records; `RpcPi.stop` removed files while the child ran; mock counted unexpected GETs as monitoring → fixed.

**#176 prototype** — dedup/backoff tests asserted less than claimed → fixed or claim dropped; the remaining prototype simplifications are listed in the capability research doc.

**Restored coverage from #182**: interrupted-liability recovery regression; exact projection count.

## Accepted residuals (documented in the plan)

- Approval write and attempt reservation are two serialized transactions; a retry landing between them can still leave a recorded approval.
- A late terminal acknowledgement after its cycle detached cannot register a monitor record; the outcome is retained and shown by status, without a notice.
- Owner liveness is pid-based; pid reuse after a crash is the foundation's existing limit.

## Gates (local)

`pnpm run check`, `pnpm run test` (1087 passed), pi-exa coverage (lines 93.6%, branches 86.7%), MCP build, changelog check, audit. Stash untouched.

**What got reviewed and fixed**
- All 6 original PRs were reviewed: 59 findings. Every production finding is fixed in #183. The prototype findings were either fixed (two tests claimed more than they checked) or written down as known prototype limits.
- #183 itself was then reviewed: 10 more findings, all fixed with regression tests.
- The worst bugs found:
  - `submit` with no active cycle quietly ran a paid standalone Agent call.
  - The same completion notice could be delivered twice.

- The approval write and the attempt reservation are separate steps. A retry landing between them can leave an approval saved with no attempt.
- Owner liveness uses process IDs, so a reused process ID after a crash can look alive. This limit predates the stack.

- **Guided consent hardening (review).** `researchMode: "submit"` without an active cycle is refused instead of running a standalone paid Agent call; a mismatched `cycleId` is reported before anything about the active cycle; the dialog is not offered while overspend, conflicting receipts or unassessed unknown liabilities exist (`DIALOG_APPROVAL_BLOCKED`); dialog grants merge with the grant current at write time instead of lowering a wider ceiling or scope; the approval write rechecks for an attempt created while the dialog was open; a missing submitter is detected before the dialog. Provider/contact requests are no longer funded at the base price: the operator assesses the exact request by command and the dialog confirms it. A wait that expires before the create is sent is reported as not dispatched (no charge) with the explicit retry path.

- **Background monitoring hardening (review).** Notices are claimed before sending so a tick and a resume cannot both deliver one; a failed re-send keeps its possible-duplicate label; foreground-reported terminal outcomes are never notified again on resume; genuine late create acknowledgements are adopted into monitoring; storage failures anywhere in a tick pause the monitor; stale ticks never act for a re-registered monitor; a resumed dead owner's monitor moves to the resuming session; resume isolates per-attempt failures; monitors no longer pause on a vetoed switch or fork; another live runtime's monitors and notices are left alone at session start; the first backoff step now follows the first check (5 s, then 7.5 s); foreground-reported outcomes are recorded so resume still notifies a late acknowledgement that arrived after detach; other sessions' undelivered notices are summarized at start; an invalid `EXA_BASE_URL` pauses monitoring as a configuration error without echoing the value.

+- **Atomic dialog approval and pid-reuse detection.** A dialog approval and its Agent reservation are now one durable write, so an approval is never recorded without its attempt. Cycle owners and storage locks record their process start time, so a pid reused after a crash no longer makes a dead owner look alive or leaves a lock stuck.

- **Flags applied after the factory now take effect everywhere.** Tool timeouts are resolved at call time, tools disabled by a late `--exa-config-file` are withdrawn (hidden), the four planner tools share one plan across registrations, the `--exa-config` deprecation warning prints once, and `EXA_BASE_URL` must be an absolute http(s) URL.

- **Extension CLI flags are reachable by their documented names.** Pi registers flags by bare name and the CLI strips the leading dashes itself, so the `--exa-*` registrations were only reachable as `----exa-*`. `--exa-api-key`, `--exa-enable-advanced`, `--exa-enable-research`, `--exa-config-file`, `--exa-config`, `--exa-timeout-ms`, `--exa-research-timeout-ms`, `--exa-submit-timeout-ms` and `--exa-monitor-interval-ms` now parse as documented. Pi also applies flag values only after extension factories run, so tool enablement from `--exa-config-file`, `--exa-enable-advanced` and `--exa-enable-research` is now refreshed at `session_start`, registering newly enabled tools instead of silently ignoring the flags.

- **Replacement liability guards reuse the complete shared attempt floor**, including known receipt conflicts and the immutable fixed-effort base, instead of re-deriving a partial floor. Stale replacement consent is rejected before reservation without consuming permissions or changing saved history.
